method: Formal game-theoretic modeling of a team facing a reactive adversary, with commitment to response strategies, analysis of hiding costs versus adversarial objectives, a solved Gaussian model, and an exact finite-game test for when the trust-limiting strategy is optimal.
result: A committed team never loses when the opponent values its own goals more, and matches a fully informed team exactly when the opponent's stake exceeds the gain from lying; below that threshold partial trust — promising not to use all learned information — yields the truth plus the cost the opponent would have paid to conceal it.
conclusion: Information is not merely gathered or aggregated but can be produced by a team's commitment to respond, with trust allocation and redundancy among members substituting for private randomness and communication.

title: PP-Mark: Provable And Publicly Verifiable Watermarking For Generative Ai
authors: Taehoon Kim Hankyeong Ko
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI models now produce images indistinguishable from real data, making publicly verifiable provenance essential; however, existing watermarking methods become vulnerable to forgeries and adversarial optimization attacks once their detectors are made public. We propose PP-Mark, a provenance framework that anchors lightweight statistical detection to a zero-knowledge proof of the embedding process, ensuring that forged content cannot pass full verification by construction. We establish formal unforgeability under standard cryptographic assumptions and validate PP-Mark against representative baselines across two latent-diffusion models (SD2.1 and SDXL), demonstrating resistance to black-box imprint forgery, white-box optimization, and regeneration attacks while remaining practical for decentralized verification. Code is available at [URL].
tldr: PP-Mark is a provenance/watermarking framework for generative image models that combines lightweight statistical detection with a zero-knowledge proof of the embedding process to prevent forgery.
motivation: As generative models produce images indistinguishable from real data, publicly verifiable provenance is needed, but public detectors invite forgery and adversarial optimization attacks.
method: The authors anchor statistical watermark detection to a zero-knowledge proof of the embedding process, prove unforgeability under standard cryptographic assumptions, and evaluate on SD2.1 and SDXL against representative baselines.
result: PP-Mark resists black-box imprint forgery, white-box optimization, and regeneration attacks while remaining practical for decentralized verification.
conclusion: Cryptographic proofs of embedding yield provably unforgeable, publicly verifiable watermarking for generative AI, though the work lies outside quantum information science.

title: Metadevices That Compute: Mathematical Foundations And Experimental Implementations For Neuromorphic Nanophotonics
authors: Xian Hadia, Odysseas Tsilipakos, Dimitrios C. Tzarouchis, Rapha\"el Pestourie
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wave-based analog computing has re-emerged as a compelling alternative to digital electronics for specific linear-algebraic and machine-learning workloads, promising massively parallel, high-bandwidth, and energy-efficient information processing. Metamaterials, metasurfaces, and integrated metastructures (collectively, metadevices) now perform mathematical operations, solve integral and differential equations, multiply matrices, and implement trainable photonic neural networks directly in the wave domain. This focused review consolidates the mathematical foundations that underpin such devices, i.e., the mapping between linear operators and wave scattering, the feedback architectures that realize equation inversion, and the inverse-design and scientific machine-learning toolchains that make their synthesis and training tractable, and connects them to the rapidly growing body of experimental demonstrations, from free-space diffractive processors to reconfigurable guided-wave metastructures. We conclude with open problems and opportunities for this emerging neuromorphic nanophotonics ecosystem.
tldr: A focused review of metadevices (metamaterials, metasurfaces, integrated metastructures) that perform wave-based analog computing, covering the mathematical foundations linking linear operators to wave scattering and the experimental demonstrations of photonic neuromorphic processors.
motivation: Digital electronics face limits in energy efficiency and bandwidth for linear-algebraic and machine-learning workloads, motivating massively parallel, high-bandwidth analog wave-domain computation.
method: The authors consolidate the mathematical mapping between linear operators and wave scattering, feedback architectures for equation inversion, and inverse-design/scientific machine-learning toolchains, then connect these to experimental platforms ranging from free-space diffractive processors to reconfigurable guided-wave metastructures.
result: The review organizes the field into a coherent framework spanning theory, design methodology, and experimental implementations of trainable photonic neural networks and equation solvers.
conclusion: The paper outlines open problems and opportunities for the emerging neuromorphic nanophotonics ecosystem, positioning metadevices as a viable analog-computing paradigm.

title: On The Communication-Sensing Tradeoff In DMT-Optimal Space-time-Coded Isac Systems
authors: Wei-Chen Chen, Yu-Chih Huang, Ming-Chun Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) has been extensively studied from the perspective of communication-sensing performance tradeoffs. In MIMO communication systems, the diversity-multiplexing tradeoff (DMT) fundamentally characterizes the tradeoff between communication reliability and multiplexing gain, and DMT-optimal space-time codes achieve this optimal tradeoff without instantaneous channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT), making them particularly attractive for ISAC scenarios where accurate CSIT is difficult to acquire or maintain. In this work, we propose an analytical framework for characterizing the sensing behavior and communication-sensing gain tradeoff of DMT-optimal space-time codes in ISAC systems. Under a single-target detection model, we propose the sensing diversity order as the high-SNR sensing reliability metric. We further show that a class of DMT-optimal space-time codes, exemplified by Perfect codes, eliminates sensing blind spots for all nonzero codewords, thereby achieving joint DMT-sensing-diversity (DMTS) optimality. Furthermore, using the Perfect code as a representative DMT-optimal construction, we show that its isotropic average transmit covariance limits the achievable sensing gain when the target angular region is narrow. We therefore develop a full-rank spatial precoding framework and a low-complexity surrogate precoder that preserve joint DMTS optimality while shaping the transmit beampattern. Simulation results show that, for a target angular region of [MATH], the proposed design achieves approximately 3 dB sensing-gain improvement over the unprecoded Perfect code.
tldr: The paper develops an analytical framework for the sensing diversity order and communication-sensing gain tradeoff of DMT-optimal space-time codes in MIMO integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, and proposes full-rank spatial precoders that preserve joint DMTS optimality while improving beampattern gain.
motivation: DMT-optimal space-time codes operate without instantaneous CSIT, making them attractive for ISAC where channel knowledge at the transmitter is hard to obtain, but their sensing behavior and the resulting communication-sensing tradeoff were not previously characterized.
method: The authors introduce a sensing diversity order as a high-SNR sensing reliability metric under a single-target detection model, analyze Perfect codes to show elimination of sensing blind spots, and design a full-rank spatial precoding framework with a low-complexity surrogate precoder to shape the transmit beampattern while retaining DMTS optimality.
result: Perfect codes achieve joint DMT-sensing-diversity optimality, and the proposed precoding design yields roughly a 3 dB sensing-gain improvement over the unprecoded Perfect code for a narrow target angular region.
conclusion: DMT-optimal space-time coding can be made jointly optimal for sensing and communication, with precoding overcoming the sensing-gain limitation imposed by isotropic transmit covariance.

title: Merging And Evolution Of Data Bases: A Many-Logic Approach
authors: Manuel A. Martins (cidma,dep. Of Mathematics), Abilio Rodrigues
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A new approach to information-based logics using many-logic modal structures (MLMSs) was recently proposed by Martins et al. In such a setting, it is possible to have worlds with different underlying logics within the same frame, all anchored to a base lattice that contains the semantics of each logic as a down-complete sublattice. In this paper, we take the lattice L6, defined by the six-valued semantics of the logic of evidence and truth LET + K , as our base lattice. We also consider four-, three-, and two-valued formal systems associated with down-complete sublattices of L6. These logics are capable of representing paracomplete, paraconsistent, and classical contexts with six, four, three, and two informational scenarios, respectively. As applications of MLMSs, we will discuss the merging and temporal evolution of databases whose underlying logics are two-, three-, four-, and six-valued. We will also investigate inconsistency measures in this context.
tldr: The paper develops many-logic modal structures anchored on the six-valued lattice L6 of the logic of evidence and truth LET+K, and applies them to the merging and temporal evolution of databases with differing underlying logics.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the recently proposed framework of many-logic modal structures, in which different worlds within a single frame carry different underlying logics, and to demonstrate its use in modelling information systems whose components obey distinct logical regimes.
method: They take the six-valued lattice L6 as the base lattice, identify four-, three-, and two-valued systems corresponding to down-complete sublattices, and construct modal frames whose worlds are assigned these varying logics, then apply the formalism to database merging and evolution and to inconsistency measures.
result: The construction yields a hierarchy of paracomplete, paraconsistent, and classical contexts with six, four, three, and two informational scenarios, and provides a formal treatment of database merging, temporal evolution, and inconsistency measurement within that hierarchy.
conclusion: Many-logic modal structures provide a flexible semantic framework for reasoning about heterogeneous information sources, though the work is purely logical and does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Simple Cuts, Simple Landscape: Dimension-Free Rank Bounds For Burer-Monteiro Factorizations Via Rank-Width
authors: Hongjin Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study Burer-Monteiro factorizations of semidefinite programs with unit diagonal constraints. For a real symmetric cost matrix whose rank-width over [MATH] is at most [MATH], we prove that every non-flat second-order stationary point of the factorized problem is globally optimal whenever the factorization rank is at least [MATH], independently of the matrix size.
tldr: The paper proves dimension-free rank bounds for Burer-Monteiro factorizations of unit-diagonal semidefinite programs using rank-width.
motivation: Burer-Monteiro factorizations are widely used to solve semidefinite programs, but understanding when their second-order stationary points are globally optimal is important for practical and theoretical guarantees.
method: It analyzes real symmetric cost matrices with bounded rank-width and shows that every non-flat second-order stationary point of the factorized problem is globally optimal for sufficiently large factorization rank.
result: The required factorization rank depends only on the rank-width parameter and is independent of the matrix size.
conclusion: The work provides dimension-free optimality guarantees for Burer-Monteiro factorizations under rank-width assumptions.

title: Dimension Changes The Scale-Signal Channel In Nearest-Neighbor Two-Sample Testing
authors: Hao Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nearest-neighbor two-sample tests are often analyzed with dimension fixed. We study the power of the generalized edge-count test on a directed 1-nearest-neighbor graph. This statistic combines a weighted sum and a difference of the two within-sample edge counts. For balanced isotropic Gaussian samples with [MATH], we derive the connection probabilities under local location and scale alternatives. Under location alternatives, the two counts have equal mean shifts, which cancel in their difference. Under scale alternatives, the two counts instead have mean shifts of opposite signs. We also derive the growth rate of the null expectation [MATH], where [MATH] counts pairs of directed edges sharing exactly one vertex. On an explicit range of [MATH], we establish local-power limits strictly above the test level for scale alternatives in the difference component at the scale [MATH]. Here [MATH] gives the variance order of the difference count under these local alternatives. At this scale, the standardized drift of the weighted sum vanishes. When [MATH], the weighted component instead detects local Gaussian scale alternatives while the difference component has no limiting drift. Thus dimension changes both the magnitude of a detectable scale difference and the component of the test that detects it.
tldr: A purely classical statistics paper analyzing how data dimension reshapes the power of nearest-neighbor two-sample tests on directed 1-NN graphs, separating the scale-alternative signal into weighted-sum and difference components.
motivation: Nearest-neighbor two-sample tests are typically studied with the dimension held fixed, leaving open how high-dimensional scaling alters which test component carries detectable signal.
method: Derives connection probabilities for balanced isotropic Gaussian samples under local location and scale alternatives, along with the growth rate of the null expectation of the shared-vertex edge-pair count and variance orders of the difference statistic.
result: Under location alternatives the two within-sample edge counts shift equally and cancel in the difference, whereas under scale alternatives they shift oppositely; on an explicit dimension range the difference component achieves local power strictly above the test level, while at other dimensions the weighted sum detects scale alternatives instead.
conclusion: Dimension determines both the magnitude of a detectable scale difference and which component of the generalized edge-count test detects it.

title: OrionLink: Single Sign-On With Oblivious Identity Brokers
authors: Yijia Fang, Bingyu Li, Luchao Jin, Jingqiang Lin, Mingxun Zhou, Zhijintong Zhang, Linghui Li, Qianhong Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single Sign-On (SSO) is a federated authentication mechanism that improves user experience by enabling access to multiple services, or Relying Parties (RPs), through a single authentication at an Identity Provider (IdP). To reduce integration complexity, many RPs rely on third-party Identity Brokers (Brokers) that aggregate numerous IdPs into a unified interface, thereby simplifying protocol management and interoperability. However, while brokers ease development, they introduce a fundamental security and privacy risk: sensitive authentication credentials and user behavioral data are exposed to the broker, creating a high-value single point of failure. Existing SSO solutions provide limited protection against these risks. With the goal of achieving broker obliviousness, we address these challenges at their root and present OrionLink, a comprehensive privacy-enhancing SSO pipeline that is compatible with existing brokered SSO architectures and systematically mitigates broker-induced risks without sacrificing usability. OrionLink incorporates two core components: (a) an anonymous pseudonym derivation scheme that generates unlinkable, per-RP identifiers to prevent cross-service user tracking; (b) an anonymous key exchange protocol that establishes end-to-end encrypted channels to protect user data from broker visibility. We further instantiate OrionLink with two new features, preserving broker functionality and deployability. We implemented a prototype of OrionLink within a brokered SSO environment, and experimental evaluation shows that the framework achieves substantial security and privacy improvements with acceptable performance overhead.
tldr: OrionLink is a privacy-enhancing single sign-on pipeline that hides user identities and authentication data from third-party identity brokers.
motivation: Brokered SSO improves usability and integration but concentrates sensitive credentials and behavioral data at the broker, creating privacy and security risks.
method: The system combines anonymous pseudonym derivation for unlinkable per-relying-party identifiers with an anonymous key exchange protocol for end-to-end encrypted channels that brokers cannot inspect.
result: A prototype implementation in a brokered SSO environment shows improved security and privacy with acceptable performance overhead.
conclusion: OrionLink mitigates broker-induced tracking and credential exposure while preserving broker functionality and deployability.

title: Variational Surface Matching For Multichannel Molecular Photoionization
authors: Carlos Marante, Vicent J Borr\`as, Jes\'us Gonz\'alez V\'azquez, Fernando Mart\'in, Luca Argenti
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an improved method for computing multichannel scattering states in the \ASTRA{} (AttoSecond TRAnsitions) molecular ionization code. Our pole-free Galerkin method with variational surface matching (PFG-VSM) yields a boundary response that is stationary with respect to errors in the interior wave function. Compared with matching based on directly evaluated radial derivatives, this formulation yields substantially faster convergence and greater numerical stability as the number of open channels increases. Comparison with a numerical solution of the exactly separable [MATH] problem establishes the accuracy attainable in a hybrid Gaussian--B-spline basis for a polycentric potential, independently of many-electron close-coupling approximations. A direct comparison of the two matching prescriptions for CO demonstrates the stability of the variational formulation under radial-basis coarsening. For neon, agreement with the NewStock atomic ionization code tests the treatment of the continuum degeneracies that arise when rotational symmetry is represented in [MATH]. The excellent agreement with the independent \XCHEM{} molecular ionization code for CO partial cross sections and molecular-frame photoelectron angular distributions, both away from and across resonances, is a strong confirmation of the correctness of both codes. A comparison for pyrazine extends this validation to a larger polyatomic target.
tldr: An improved numerical method (PFG-VSM) for computing multichannel molecular photoionization scattering states in the ASTRA code, validated against independent atomic and molecular ionization codes.
motivation: Multichannel scattering-state calculations with polycentric potentials require stable, rapidly convergent boundary matching, especially as the number of open channels grows and correlation is treated beyond separable approximations.
method: A pole-free Galerkin scheme with variational surface matching yields a boundary response stationary with respect to interior wavefunction errors; implemented in a hybrid Gaussian–B-spline basis and benchmarked against an exactly separable solution and the NewStock and XCHEM codes.
result: The variational matching converges substantially faster and is more stable under radial-basis coarsening than direct radial-derivative matching, and reproduces CO partial cross sections, molecular-frame photoelectron angular distributions, and neon degeneracy handling in good agreement with independent codes, including pyrazine.
conclusion: The variational surface matching formulation provides a robust, accurate approach for multichannel molecular ionization calculations, though the work is a computational/numerical methods contribution in molecular photoionization rather than quantum information science.

title: Comparison Of Melanin Subtypes Using Pump-probe Microscopy
authors: Emma Bao, David Grass, Martin C. Fischer, Warren S. Warren
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pump-probe microscopy (PPM) is used to probe excited state dynamics of endogenous chromophores to generate contrast that is unavailable in traditional forms of microscopy. Here we apply PPM to characterize melanin, a pigment central to photoprotection, skin and eye pigmentation, and melanoma pathogenesis. Melanin is notoriously difficult to analyze due to its structural and chemical complexity. We imaged melanin from six different lesion categories: cutaneous nevi, lentigo, cutaneous malignant melanoma, conjunctival melanocytic lesions, vulvar melanocytic lesions, and a murine melanoma model, across 21 independent biological samples and 109 regions of interest. Using model fitting, adapted phasor analysis, and support vector machine classification, we characterize and quantify excited-state dynamics as a surrogate for chemical and structural heterogeneity. Heterogeneity of melanin separates cutaneous from non-cutaneous lesions, but is not correlated with malignancy. Benign lentigo is the most heterogeneous population in the dataset, exceeding cutaneous malignant melanoma, while conjunctival lesions are the most homogeneous despite receiving direct solar exposure. Classification on full transient absorption curves separates most subtypes well above the six-class chance level. These findings demonstrate the ability of PPM to reveal subtle differences in melanin photophysics across diverse tissue environments, with implications for optical tissue classification and the understanding of melanoma pathogenesis.
tldr: Pump-probe microscopy is used to characterize excited-state dynamics of melanin from six lesion categories and classify melanin subtypes via model fitting, phasor analysis, and SVM.
motivation: Melanin is structurally and chemically complex and hard to analyze, yet central to photoprotection, pigmentation, and melanoma pathogenesis, motivating label-free optical contrast methods.
method: Pump-probe microscopy of 21 biological samples and 109 regions of interest, combined with model fitting, adapted phasor analysis, and support vector machine classification of transient absorption curves.
result: Melanin heterogeneity separates cutaneous from non-cutaneous lesions but does not correlate with malignancy; benign lentigo is the most heterogeneous and conjunctival lesions the most homogeneous; classification separates most subtypes well above six-class chance.
conclusion: PPM reveals subtle differences in melanin photophysics across tissue environments, with implications for optical tissue classification and understanding of melanoma pathogenesis.

title: Generalized Supremum Convolutions On The Tensor Product Of Unit Intervals: T-conorms And Triangle Functions
authors: Mengyu Luo, Lili Shen, Jie Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The complete-lattice tensor product [MATH] arises naturally in the algebra of truth values for type-2 fuzzy sets. For a monotone surjective map [MATH] that is continuous on [MATH] and a monotone map [MATH] having [MATH] as identity, we consider the generalized supremum convolution \[ (f\otimes_{_{S,T}}g)(x)=\sup_{S(u,v)=x}T(f(u),g(v)) \] on [MATH]. Rather than assuming classical algebraic structures for [MATH] and [MATH] from the outset, we ask when they are forced by requiring the induced convolution itself to be a t-conorm. We prove that [MATH] is a t-conorm on [MATH] if and only if [MATH] is a continuous t-conorm and either [MATH] or [MATH] is a right-continuous t-norm; in the exceptional case [MATH], the convolution is simply the pointwise maximum for every admissible [MATH]. The same convolution mechanism also yields an order-dual description of triangle functions on the space of distance distribution functions [MATH]. Using an order-reversing isomorphism between [MATH] and a boundary variant of [MATH], we show that [MATH] is a triangle function precisely when [MATH] is a continuous t-conorm with no zero divisor and, unless [MATH], [MATH] is a left-continuous t-conorm; moreover, when [MATH], continuity of [MATH] is equivalent to continuity of [MATH]. This resolves the remaining [MATH] part of the Schweizer--Sklar problem.
tldr: The paper studies generalized supremum convolutions on tensor products of unit intervals and characterizes when they yield t-conorms or triangle functions, resolving part of the Schweizer–Sklar problem.
motivation: These algebraic structures arise in the truth-value algebra of type-2 fuzzy sets and in probabilistic metric spaces, motivating a systematic characterization of when the convolution operation preserves t-conorm or triangle-function structure.
method: The authors define a generalized supremum convolution using monotone maps S and T on the unit interval and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the resulting operation to be a t-conorm or a triangle function, using an order-reversing isomorphism.
result: They prove that the convolution is a t-conorm iff S is a continuous t-conorm and either S or T is a right-continuous t-norm, with an exceptional case yielding pointwise maximum; they also characterize triangle functions via continuous t-conorms with no zero divisor and left-continuity conditions.
conclusion: The work resolves the remaining case of the Schweizer–Sklar problem and provides an order-dual description linking t-conorms and triangle functions on distance distribution functions.

title: Beyond Left-continuity: T-norms On The Fuzzy Unit Interval Induced By Pairs Of T-norms
authors: Rongjun Wu, Jie Sun, Hongliang Lai
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a binary operation [MATH] on the fuzzy unit interval [MATH] by extending the natural action of [MATH] and [MATH] on step functions. When both [MATH] and [MATH] are left-continuous, this operation coincides with the tensor product of the corresponding quantales and therefore yields a t-norm on [MATH]. Without left-continuity, the situation becomes more subtle. We prove that if at least one of the two t-norms is continuous, then [MATH] is still a t-norm on [MATH]. We also show by counterexample that continuity cannot simply be dropped. The operation [MATH] fails to be associative. On the other hand, [MATH] is a t-norm despite [MATH] being neither continuous nor left-continuous, indicating that continuity is not a necessary condition.
tldr: The paper constructs and studies a binary operation on the fuzzy unit interval induced by pairs of t-norms, analyzing when it yields a t-norm depending on continuity assumptions.
motivation: The work extends the connection between t-norms on the fuzzy unit interval and tensor products of quantales beyond the left-continuous setting.
method: The authors define an operation on fuzzy unit interval by extending the natural action on step functions, then prove conditions under which the operation is a t-norm, including cases where at least one t-norm is continuous, and provide a counterexample when continuity is dropped.
result: The operation coincides with the quantale tensor product when both t-norms are left-continuous, remains a t-norm if at least one t-norm is continuous, but can fail to be associative; continuity is shown not to be necessary via an example.
conclusion: The paper clarifies the role of continuity in inducing t-norms on the fuzzy unit interval and demonstrates subtleties beyond the left-continuous case.

title: The Nodally Bound-preserving Finite Element Method For The Transport Equation
authors: Nicol\'as Espinoza-Contreras, Gabriel Barrenechea, Douglas Pacheco
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Numerical approximations of transport problems, even when stabilised, often violate the bounds respected by the exact solution. Depending on the problem being solved, this can produce non-physical results, such as negative densities or higher-than-unity concentrations. Various bound-preserving numerical methods exist, yet they are usually either conditionally stable or only first-order accurate. In this context, the present work extends the nodally bound-preserving finite element method to the linear transport equation. As a baseline discretisation we use the least-squares finite element method, which is instrumental in achieving unconditional stability for second-order time stepping. It also leads to symmetric algebraic systems, thereby enabling simple, efficient solvers, which we further enhance through Anderson acceleration. Unconditional stability is proved for the backward Euler and Crank--Nicolson discretisations. We also derive error estimates for the fully discrete second-order scheme and provide various numerical examples, including two-phase incompressible flows.
tldr: The paper extends nodally bound-preserving finite element methods to the linear transport equation using a least-squares baseline discretisation with unconditionally stable time stepping.
motivation: Standard stabilised numerical approximations of transport problems can violate physical bounds of the exact solution, producing non-physical artifacts like negative densities or concentrations above unity, and existing bound-preserving schemes are typically only conditionally stable or first-order accurate.
method: A least-squares finite-element discretisation is used as the baseline to obtain unconditionally stable second-order time stepping and symmetric algebraic systems, enhanced with Anderson acceleration; unconditional stability is proven for backward Euler and Crank-Nicolson, with error estimates for the fully discrete second-order scheme.
result: Unconditional stability is established for the backward Euler and Crank-Nicolson discretisations, error estimates are derived for the second-order fully discrete scheme, and numerical examples including two-phase incompressible flows demonstrate the approach.
conclusion: The nodally bound-preserving finite element framework provides a stable, higher-order, and physically consistent numerical method for linear transport problems, with potential applicability to flow simulations.

title: Addendum To "Optimal Steering Of A Linear Stochastic System To A Final Probability Distribution, Part Ii"
authors: Yongxin Chen, Tryphon T. Georgiou, Michele Pavon
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We hereby fill in a gap in an induction argument used in the proof of a theorem on state-covariance controllability of linear stochastic systems in an earlier paper by the authors. The mathematical statement is true. The missing point in the proof concerns the assertion that, in the canonical single-input case, the control can be assigned arbitrary endpoint values. We amend the argument by proving a slightly stronger induction statement that permits arbitrary finite endpoint jets of the control. An independent approach to homogeneous state-covariance controllability was provided in a paper by Abdelgalil and Georgiou (2025) as a corollary of strong controllability results on [MATH], and shown herein that it extends to the case of additive noise as well.
tldr: An addendum fixing a gap in an induction argument proving state-covariance controllability of linear stochastic systems.
motivation: The authors' earlier theorem on steering a linear stochastic system to a final probability distribution relied on an induction step asserting that controls in the canonical single-input case can take arbitrary endpoint values, which was not fully justified.
method: They prove a slightly stronger induction statement allowing arbitrary finite endpoint jets of the control, and they connect this to an independent strong-controllability approach of Abdelgalil and Georgiou, extending it to additive noise.
result: The original mathematical statement is confirmed correct, with the missing step now rigorously established and the alternative controllability route shown to cover the additive-noise case.
conclusion: The addendum repairs a technical proof gap in classical stochastic control theory, with no bearing on quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, or quantum hardware.

title: Incremental Stability Of Gradient Flows Under Generalized Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz Inequalities And Its Implications For General Systems
authors: Andreas Oliveira, Arthur C. B. de Oliveira, Mario Sznaier, Eduardo Sontag
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gradient flows of twice continuously differentiable strongly convex and convex objectives are, respectively, incrementally exponentially stable and non-expansive in the Euclidean metric. In this work, we investigate to what extent these properties extend to nonconvex objectives satisfying generalized Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz inequalities. For objectives with a unique minimizer, we establish conditions under which the gradient flow is contracting in a state-dependent Riemannian metric and incrementally exponentially stable. For objectives with nonunique minimizers, we generalize the non-expansivity of convex objectives to incremental stability for more general nonconvex objectives. We focus on incremental stability due to its implication to convergence to equilibrium points; when paired with a Lyapunov function it implies pointwise convergence to a minimizer and continuity of the endpoint map. Along the way, we derive new structural results for incrementally stable nonlinear systems and extend the analysis to Heavy-Ball and Dynamical Inertial Newton flows.
tldr: The paper studies incremental stability and contractivity of gradient flows for nonconvex objectives satisfying generalized Polyak-Łojasiewicz inequalities, including Heavy-Ball and Dynamical Inertial Newton flows.
motivation: Strongly convex objectives yield incrementally exponentially stable gradient flows, but it is unclear to what extent these attractive stability properties survive for nonconvex objectives that only satisfy PL-type conditions.
method: The authors derive structural results for incrementally stable nonlinear systems and construct state-dependent Riemannian metrics under which gradient flows of PL-type objectives are contracting, using Lyapunov arguments to link incremental stability to convergence.
result: For uniquely-minimizing objectives they give conditions for contraction and incremental exponential stability; for non-unique minimizers they extend non-expansivity of convex objectives to incremental stability, implying pointwise convergence and continuity of the endpoint map.
conclusion: Incremental stability provides a unified lens for convergence analysis of gradient and inertial flows beyond convexity, with extensions to Heavy-Ball and Dynamical Inertial Newton dynamics.

title: Learning Stabilizing Latent Feedback Controllers Via Multi-Step Backward Losses
authors: Paul Lutkus, Lars Lindemann, Stephen Tu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can learned latent dynamics models support the design of feedback controllers that provably stabilize the original system? For linear time-invariant systems, we show that learning linear autoencoders and latent dynamics with multi-step prediction-reconstruction losses [MATH] which we term "backward losses" as they encourage latent trajectories to reconstruct full state trajectories [MATH] provably recovers the structure needed for stabilization. Specifically, a sufficiently long reconstruction horizon ensures that a minimum [MATH]-norm controller designed using the learned latent model stabilizes the original system through output-feedback via the corresponding encoder, provided the latent dimension is large enough to capture all non-stable modes of the underlying system. We also show why both reconstruction and a multi-step horizon are essential: forward prediction losses that require only low prediction error along latent trajectories admit global loss minimizers that discard unstable modes regardless of horizon length, while single-step reconstruction losses can yield latent models whose stabilizing controllers fail to stabilize the original system. Finally, experiments on a non-linear flexible-arm system illustrate the practical implications of our results for learning non-linear autoencoders and latent dynamics.
tldr: The paper proves that learning linear autoencoders and latent dynamics with multi-step 'backward' prediction-reconstruction losses provably yields latent models whose minimum-norm controllers stabilize the original LTI system via output feedback.
motivation: Learned latent dynamics models are attractive for control, but it is unclear when a controller designed in latent space actually stabilizes the true system; the authors aim to give conditions under which this holds.
method: They analyze linear time-invariant systems, learning a linear encoder/decoder plus latent dynamics with multi-step reconstruction losses, and characterize when the latent dimension and reconstruction horizon suffice to retain all non-stable modes; they also construct counterexamples for forward-prediction and single-step losses.
result: A sufficiently long reconstruction horizon and large enough latent dimension guarantee that a minimum-norm latent controller stabilizes the original system through the encoder, while forward-prediction or single-step reconstruction losses can provably discard unstable modes or fail to stabilize.
conclusion: Multi-step backward reconstruction losses are essential for reliable latent-space controller design, illustrated experimentally on a nonlinear flexible-arm system.

title: Neural Network Methods In The 2bsde Formalism For Solving The High-Dimensional Black--Scholes Equation With Transaction Costs
authors: Guhesh Kumaran
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A 2BSDE system is written down for a [MATH]-dimensional Black--Scholes partial differential equation (PDE) with the Leland transaction cost model which incorporates the sign of the curvature. The 2BSDE system takes input from the ``speed'' (derivative of the curvature). This system is solved using a single ResNet neural network which learns both the solution to the PDE as well as the degrees of freedom in the curvature matrix. The network is used to learn the price of derivatives such as call options and butterfly spreads on geometric baskets for [MATH] achieving a time-averaged RMSE of less than [MATH] in each case.
tldr: The paper formulates a 2BSDE system for a high-dimensional Black-Scholes PDE with Leland transaction costs and solves it using a ResNet neural network.
motivation: It aims to price derivatives under transaction costs in high dimensions, where standard PDE methods become intractable.
method: A second-order backward stochastic differential equation system incorporating curvature and its derivative is solved with a single ResNet that learns both the PDE solution and curvature degrees of freedom.
result: The method prices call options and butterfly spreads on geometric baskets in high dimensions, achieving time-averaged RMSE below prescribed thresholds in each case.
conclusion: Neural-network-based 2BSDE methods provide a practical approach to high-dimensional option pricing with transaction costs, but the work is unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Stochastic And Noisy Oracles In Smooth Continuous Optimization
authors: Albert S. Berahas, Liyuan Cao, Katya Scheinberg
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We review models of inexact computational oracles in smooth continuous optimization and their implications for the convergence, computational complexity, and attainable accuracy of optimization algorithms. We adopt a framework in which zeroth-,first-, and second-order oracles are characterized by quantitative error bounds and may accept additional control parameters that influence both their accuracy and computational cost. We introduce deterministic and stochastic oracle models and illustrate their properties through a variety of examples, including finite-difference approximations, stochastic gradients, and randomized derivative estimators. Particular attention is given to the distinction between absolute and relative errors, bias and variance, and stochastic function evaluations with independent or coupled randomness. A central theme of the review is the use of common analytical tools to recover and compare convergence and complexity guarantees under different oracle models. For deterministic and stochastic first-order methods, we show how a general descent inequality leads to complexity bounds under various assumptions on the objective function and all proposed oracle models. In the stochastic setting, we develop bounds on expected stopping times and the accuracy that can be guaranteed under different oracle conditions. We also examine the total computational complexity of algorithms relying on specific oracle constructions and briefly review models of inexact second- order information and their use in optimization algorithms.
tldr: A review of inexact deterministic and stochastic oracle models in smooth continuous optimization and their implications for convergence, complexity, and attainable accuracy.
motivation: Optimization algorithms in practice rely on noisy or approximate gradient, function, and Hessian information, so a unified framework is needed to compare convergence guarantees across different oracle models.
method: The authors formalize zeroth-, first-, and second-order oracles via quantitative error bounds with tunable control parameters, distinguish absolute vs relative error and bias vs variance, and derive complexity bounds from a common descent inequality.
result: Unified convergence and complexity guarantees are recovered for deterministic and stochastic first-order methods, including bounds on expected stopping times and achievable accuracy for finite differences, stochastic gradients, and randomized derivative estimators.
conclusion: Common analytical tools allow systematic comparison of oracle models, clarifying how oracle accuracy and cost trade off against algorithmic complexity and final solution quality.

title: Sharp Solyanik Estimates For Discrete And Ergodic Hardy--Littlewood Maximal Operators
authors: Kesen Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations of a probability space, and let [MATH] denote the sharp Tauberian constant of the associated ergodic uncentered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator. Hagelstein and Parissis showed that [MATH] as [MATH] and asked whether this exponent is sharp. We prove that [MATH] for all such transformations, and that this is sharp: equality of the ergodic and discrete Tauberian constants holds for every action admitting arbitrarily large Rokhlin towers (in particular for every free action, ergodic or not), and the discrete constant satisfies [MATH]. For [MATH] the sharp ergodic exponent [MATH] is strictly smaller than the sharp Euclidean exponent [MATH] recently obtained by Mukherjee; the discrepancy is caused by a lattice ``first layer'' effect. We also show that the discrete Tauberian constants of the Hardy--Littlewood and strong maximal operators dominate their Euclidean counterparts; for the strong maximal operator this yields [MATH] for every free action.
tldr: The paper studies sharp Tauberian constants for ergodic and discrete Hardy--Littlewood maximal operators under commuting measure-preserving transformations.
motivation: Hagelstein and Parissis established an asymptotic bound for the ergodic Tauberian constant and asked whether the exponent is sharp; this work resolves that question.
method: The author proves bounds for ergodic and discrete Tauberian constants, shows sharpness via Rokhlin towers, and compares ergodic exponents with Euclidean counterparts.
result: The sharp ergodic exponent is established and shown to be strictly smaller than the sharp Euclidean exponent for dimension two, due to a lattice first-layer effect; discrete constants are also shown to dominate Euclidean ones for Hardy--Littlewood and strong maximal operators.
conclusion: The results settle the sharpness question and clarify differences between ergodic, discrete, and Euclidean maximal operator constants.

title: Post-mimo: Partition-Oriented Semantic Transmission For Mimo Point Cloud Delivery
authors: Hang Yue, Junlin Chang, Tianqing Zhao, Yulin Zhao, Rongke Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Point clouds have become a fundamental data format for emerging three dimensional (3D) applications, while their wireless delivery remains challenging due to the large data volume and irregular geometric structure. Existing semantic point cloud transmission methods are mainly developed for single-input single-output systems, making them difficult to apply directly to multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. To address this issue, we propose a partition-oriented semantic transmission framework for MIMO (POST-MIMO) point cloud delivery. POST-MIMO partitions the input point cloud into spatially coherent blocks and aligns them with parallel MIMO streams. Based on this block-aligned representation, the transmitter employs a hierarchical encoder to capture both intra-block local geometry and inter-block global dependency, while the auxiliary side information is transmitted jointly to assist reconstruction. At the receiver, a progressive decoder reconstructs the block geometry in a progressive manner and restores the final point cloud with block-aware adjustment. Experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction quality and lower computational resource consumption than representative reference schemes under the considered MIMO setting.
tldr: POST-MIMO proposes a partition-oriented semantic transmission framework that splits point clouds into spatially coherent blocks mapped onto parallel MIMO streams for wireless 3D delivery.
motivation: Point clouds are large and irregular, and existing semantic point cloud transmission schemes are designed for single-input single-output links, so they do not transfer directly to MIMO systems.
method: The input cloud is partitioned into spatially coherent blocks aligned with MIMO streams; a hierarchical encoder captures intra-block geometry and inter-block dependencies, side information is sent jointly, and a progressive block-aware decoder reconstructs the cloud.
result: Experiments report better reconstruction quality and lower computational resource consumption than representative reference schemes in the considered MIMO setting.
conclusion: Block-aligned semantic coding is an effective way to adapt semantic point cloud delivery to MIMO links, improving quality-efficiency trade-offs for 3D wireless applications.

title: Discrete Total Variation Under The Multinomial, Part 3: Expectation Under A General Distribution
authors: Neven Elezovi\'c Nikola Bani\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For multinomial counts [MATH] on [MATH] ordered bins and a reference law [MATH] we study the expectation of the reference-centered discrete total variation [MATH], the natural extension of the comb-test statistic to a non-uniform null. For a non-uniform null the raw total variation of the counts carries a deterministic staircase of order [MATH] that no centering of the statistic removes; the counts are therefore centered at the reference law, and under the null ([MATH]) the statistic is the matched [MATH]. Exact finite-sample expectations are obtained by conditioning on the total mass in each adjacent pair, which reduces every edge to a translated binomial absolute-deviation problem. For fixed [MATH] and a sampling law bounded away from the boundary of the simplex, the matched statistic admits a three-term asymptotic expansion in powers of [MATH] whose coefficients are explicit continuous periodic functions of [MATH] (a generalized, non-Poincar\'e asymptotic expansion), obtained by a weighted local Edgeworth estimate and a corner Euler--Maclaurin summation; all half-integer orders vanish by parity. Each correction separates into a smooth Edgeworth part and an oscillatory lattice part, the latter an Edgeworth perturbation of one formal Euler--Maclaurin series of a Gaussian lattice sum. Under a sampling law [MATH] the leading expectation is the folded-normal profile implied by the central limit theorem; under local alternatives we identify the [MATH] correction (a skewness term, plus a variance-gradient term for Pitman alternatives), and fixed alternatives give a law-of-large-numbers limit, the [MATH] distance between the adjacent-gradient profiles of [MATH] and [MATH], on which threshold tests are consistent.
tldr: This paper derives asymptotic and finite-sample expectations for a reference-centered discrete total variation statistic of multinomial counts.
motivation: The authors aim to extend comb-test statistics to non-uniform null distributions, where raw total variation has a deterministic staircase artifact that centering does not remove.
method: They condition on adjacent-pair total mass to reduce edge contributions to translated binomial absolute-deviation problems, then use weighted local Edgeworth estimates and corner Euler--Maclaurin summation to obtain asymptotic expansions.
result: The matched statistic admits a three-term asymptotic expansion with explicit periodic coefficients; local alternatives yield a skewness correction and variance-gradient term, while fixed alternatives give a law-of-large-numbers limit.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed probabilistic analysis of discrete total variation under multinomial sampling, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sparse Descent subspace-Newton Thresholding Algorithm For Sparse Optimization Problems
authors: Zhong-Feng Sun, Nan Meng, Yun-Bin Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a sparse descent direction derived from the Newton direction within a low-dimensional subspace for sparse optimization problems. Building upon this direction and incorporating hard thresholding and orthogonal projection, we develop a novel algorithm termed the sparse descent subspace-Newton thresholding (SDSNT) algorithm. We further establish its global convergence under the restricted isometry property [MATH] of the measurement matrix. Numerical experiments on random sparse vector recovery and audio signal reconstruction reveal that SDSNT achieves comparable performance to several state-of-the-art algorithms. Notably, relative to most of them, it delivers superior recovery at high sparsity levels and improved efficiency at low sparsity levels.
tldr: The paper introduces SDSNT, a sparse descent subspace-Newton thresholding algorithm for sparse optimization that combines a low-dimensional subspace Newton direction with hard thresholding and orthogonal projection.
motivation: Sparse optimization (e.g., compressed sensing recovery) benefits from efficient algorithms that exploit second-order information while respecting sparsity constraints, and the authors aim to improve recovery performance especially at high sparsity levels.
method: A sparse descent direction is derived from the Newton direction restricted to a low-dimensional subspace; this is combined with hard thresholding and orthogonal projection to form the SDSNT iterative algorithm, whose global convergence is proven under a restricted isometry property condition.
result: Numerical experiments on random sparse vector recovery and audio signal reconstruction show SDSNT is comparable to state-of-the-art methods, with better recovery at high sparsity and improved efficiency at low sparsity.
conclusion: SDSNT offers a competitive, provably convergent approach for sparse optimization, though the work lies in classical signal processing and numerical optimization rather than quantum information science.

title: RapidDOC: Riccati-Preconditioned Implicit Differentiation For Differentiable Optimal Control Under Operator Mismatch
authors: Xiangda Zhu, Yuankun Chen, Zifei Nie, Yi Chang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Differentiable optimal control embeds constrained optimization problems in data-driven pipelines by differentiating their optimality conditions and propagating task-loss gradients to model or objective parameters. A key observation is that forward optimization and backward sensitivity computation involve related stage-structured linear systems, making reuse of forward factorization information natural. However, direct reuse is generally invalid, because differences in linearization, barrier terms, regularization, and curvature can create a mismatch between the retained forward operator and the target operator defining the derivative. We therefore propose RapidDOC, a factorization-reuse method that leaves the target adjoint equation unchanged. The retained cache produces a candidate adjoint and, when its target residual exceeds the prescribed tolerance, serves as a fixed right preconditioner for GMRES. A cache-action error operator characterizes directional exactness, the preconditioned iteration, and the relation between target residual and outer-gradient error. An ablation on three constrained robotic OCPs shows that the proposed method achieves lower backward time than both target-system refactorization and a no-reuse iterative method, demonstrating the computational benefit of reusing the retained forward factorizations. Across open- and closed-loop parameter-learning experiments, the proposed method achieves learning performance comparable to the baselines, while yielding the lowest open-loop backward time on all three tasks and reducing total closed-loop solver-call time by 40.5-83.1% relative to the fastest competing method. Finally, deploying the learned controller on a physical vehicle reduces the median figure-eight tracking RMSE from 22.75 to 6.09 cm, demonstrating its potential for hardware deployment.
tldr: RapidDOC accelerates differentiable optimal control by reusing forward factorization as a fixed right preconditioner for GMRES when the cached operator mismatches the target adjoint system.
motivation: Differentiable optimal control requires solving backward sensitivity systems whose structure resembles the forward optimization, but naive factorization reuse fails due to linearization, barrier, regularization, and curvature mismatches.
method: The authors retain the forward factorization, form a candidate adjoint, and when its residual exceeds tolerance use the cached operator as a right preconditioner for GMRES, with an error operator analysis bounding target residual versus outer-gradient error.
result: On three constrained robotic optimal control problems, the method yields the lowest backward times and reduces closed-loop solver-call time by 40.5-83.1% versus the fastest baseline, while physical vehicle deployment cut figure-eight tracking RMSE from 22.75 to 6.09 cm.
conclusion: Preconditioned reuse of forward factorizations gives practical speedups for differentiable optimal control without sacrificing learning performance, enabling real-time hardware deployment.

title: "Shall We Approve?" Consequence-Aware Approval For Autonomous Coding Agents
authors: Weiheng Wu, Junkai Chen, Zhensu Sun, Jieke Shi, Yunbo Lyu, David Lo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents increasingly rely on automated approvers to decide whether a proposed shell command may run. Existing approvers, from rule-based checkers to guardrail models and deployed permission classifiers, base their decisions on the text of the request and command. Yet a command's behavior depends on the code it invokes and the state of the workspace, and systems that observe file changes leave the assessment to the agent or a human after execution. We present Caper, a consequence-aware approval mechanism that pre-executes each command in a snapshotted sandbox, provides an independent approver with a bounded report of its observed effects, commits allowed commands, and rolls back blocked ones with a reason the agent can act on. Compared with six existing systems, Caper achieves the lowest harmful-outcome rate on SABER (6.7% versus at least 14.8%) and YoloFS-Ext, a benchmark we build in which harmful behavior is hidden inside invoked tools (7.8% versus at least 35.3%), while blocking 1.0% of the safe twins of the dangerous tasks in YoloFS-Ext.
tldr: Caper is a consequence-aware approval mechanism that pre-executes shell commands in a snapshotted sandbox and reports observed effects to an independent approver before committing or rolling back.
motivation: Existing automated approvers for coding agents judge commands only from request text, ignoring the invoked code and workspace state, so harmful behavior can hide inside tools.
method: Each proposed command is executed in a sandboxed snapshot, a bounded effect report is given to an independent approver, and allowed commands are committed while blocked ones are rolled back with an actionable reason.
result: Caper achieves the lowest harmful-outcome rate on SABER (6.7% vs ≥14.8%) and on the new YoloFS-Ext benchmark (7.8% vs ≥35.3%), while blocking only 1.0% of safe twins.
conclusion: Consequence-aware sandboxed pre-execution improves the safety of autonomous coding agents compared with text-based approvers, at modest cost to safe-task throughput.

title: Uniform Non-Deterministic Semantics For Ciuciura's $mbC^n$-Hierarchy
authors: Pawel Pawlowski Ela Drozdowska
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a uniform non-deterministic semantics for the hierarchy of paraconsistent systems mbC^n introduced by Ciuciura. The proposed construction generalizes Omori's three-valued semantics for mbC^1 to all systems of the hierarchy. We prove soundness and completeness of the semantics with respect to the corresponding axiomatizations and show that the consequence relations of the systems mbC^n cannot be characterized by finite deterministic matrices.
tldr: The paper introduces a uniform non-deterministic semantics for Ciuciura's hierarchy of paraconsistent logics mbC^n, proving soundness and completeness and showing the consequence relations admit no finite deterministic matrix characterization.
motivation: The mbC^n hierarchy of paraconsistent systems lacked a uniform semantic framework; only Omori's three-valued semantics for the base system mbC^1 existed, so a general semantics covering the whole hierarchy was needed.
method: The authors construct a generalization of Omori's three-valued non-deterministic semantics to all levels of the hierarchy, then prove soundness and completeness with respect to the corresponding axiomatizations, and finally establish a negative result about finite deterministic matrices.
result: The proposed non-deterministic semantics is shown to be sound and complete for every system mbC^n, and the consequence relations of these systems provably cannot be characterized by finite deterministic matrices.
conclusion: Non-deterministic semantics provides a uniform and adequate framework for the entire mbC^n hierarchy, while deterministic finite-valued semantics are fundamentally insufficient for these paraconsistent logics.

title: On Some Logics Intermediate Between S4.2 And S4.3 Defined By The Notion Of Independence
authors: Maciej A. Ha{\l}apacz
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hamkins and Loewe described modal logic S4.2 through the notion of sets of independent buttons - statements that are possibly necessary - and switches - necessarily contingent statements. In this article we investigate logics intermediate between S4.2 and S4.3 that are defined through a different notion of independence. We provide an axiomatic description of such logics, state some basic facts and prove various completeness and decidability results.
tldr: The paper characterizes modal logics intermediate between S4.2 and S4.3 defined via a variant notion of independence of buttons and switches, giving axioms, completeness, and decidability results.
motivation: Hamkins and Löwe gave a button-and-switch analysis of S4.2; the author asks which logics lying between S4.2 and S4.3 admit an analogous independent-button characterization.
method: Pure modal-logic techniques: axiomatic presentation of candidate systems, Kripke-frame semantics, correspondence arguments, and standard completeness/decidability proofs.
result: Axiomatic descriptions of the intermediate logics are provided, together with basic structural facts and proofs of completeness and decidability for the resulting systems.
conclusion: The independence-based approach yields a coherent family of logics strictly between S4.2 and S4.3 with good metatheoretic properties, extending the Hamkins–Löwe program.

title: On {\L}ukasiewicz Topological Semantics
authors: Muhammad Afaq Khan (cidma,department Of Mathematics, University Of Aveiro Aveiro, Portugal), Manuel A. Martins (cidma,department Of Mathematics, University Of Aveiro Aveiro, Portugal), Alexandre Madeira (cidma,department Of Mathematics, University Of Aveiro Aveiro, Portugal), Babar Zaman
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose fuzzy topological semantics for {\L}ukasiewicz valued modal logic, based on the standard {\L}ukasiewicz algebra. Within this setting, formulas are interpreted as fuzzy sets of truth values, while the modal operators are realized through fuzzy interior and closure operators. We define a Kripke-induced fuzzy Alexandroff topology and establish a precise correspondence between {\L}ukasiewicz fuzzy Kripke semantics and its topological counterpart. The proposed topological semantics validates the S4 modal axioms that include reflexivity, transitivity, monotonicity, normality, and the necessitation of truth.
tldr: The paper develops fuzzy topological semantics for Łukasiewicz-valued modal logic, interpreting formulas as fuzzy sets and modal operators as fuzzy interior and closure operators, and proves equivalence with a Kripke-style semantics.
motivation: Modal logic with many-valued (Łukasiewicz) truth degrees lacks a well-developed topological semantics, and the authors aim to supply one that mirrors the classical correspondence between Kripke frames and Alexandroff topologies.
method: They build semantics on the standard Łukasiewicz algebra, define a Kripke-induced fuzzy Alexandroff topology, and establish a correspondence theorem linking fuzzy Kripke semantics with the topological interpretation.
result: The proposed topological semantics is shown to validate the S4 axioms, including reflexivity, transitivity, monotonicity, normality, and necessitation of truth.
conclusion: The work provides a coherent topological foundation for Łukasiewicz fuzzy modal logic, though it remains a purely logical/mathematical contribution with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Paraclassical Logics With Two Negations
authors: Pawel Pawlowski (centre For Logic,philosophy Of Science Ghent University, Ghent, Belgium), Pietro Vigiani
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study three paraclassical propositional logics with two negations, CLoaN, CLouN, and CLauN, obtained by pairwise combining the one-negation systems CLuN, CLaN, and CLoN. CLuN's negation is glut-tolerant and paraconsistent, CLaN's negationis gap-tolerant and paracomplete, and CLoN's negation is both paraconsistent and paracomplete. We provide sound and complete two-valued non-deterministic semantics for each of the two-negations systems. We then focus on CLauN, the system containing the primitive dual pair of CLaN and CLuN negations. In this setting, we show deductive relationships between different negations expressible in CLauN; we show two diferent ways to recapture classical logic by means of translations, locally and globally; and we show a duality results for the multiple conclusion consequence relation of the logic.
tldr: The paper develops sound and complete two-valued non-deterministic semantics for three paraclassical propositional logics combining two negations (paraconsistent, paracomplete, and both), with a detailed study of CLauN.
motivation: Non-classical logics with gap- and glut-tolerant negations are of interest in paraconsistent logic; combining two negations into a single system allows reasoning with both paraconsistency and paracompleteness.
method: The authors define CLoaN, CLouN, and CLauN by pairwise combining the one-negation systems CLoN, CLuN, and CLaN, and construct two-valued non-deterministic (Nmatrix-style) semantics, proving soundness and completeness.
result: They establish deductive relationships among the expressible negations, give local and global translations recovering classical logic, and prove a duality result for the multiple-conclusion consequence relation of CLauN.
conclusion: CLauN provides a coherent framework hosting a dual pair of paraconsistent and paracomplete negations, with classical logic recoverable by translation.

title: Arithmetical Characterizations Of Two Intuitionistic Logical Principles
authors: Kaito Ichikura
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the role of negation in arithmetic by analyzing subsystems based on subminimal logic. We introduce NA^PR, a system of subminimal arithmetic equipped with all primitive recursive functions, and answer the following four questions: (1) Can we develop reasonable arithmetic within NA^PR? (2) Can we characterize logical rules Absorption of Negation (An) and Ex Falso Quodlibet (ECQ) by arithmetical principles? (3) Are there strict differences in deductive power among NA^PR, MA^PR, and HA? (4) Do MA^PR and MA, and NA^PR and NA have a similar mutual interpretability relationship as HA? We show the following: First, Heyting Arithmetic (HA) is shown to be a conservative extension of NA^PR for positive formulas. Based on NA^PR, we prove that (ECQ) is equivalent to the definability of disjunction, and that (An) is equivalent to a variant of the least number principle. Furthermore, using the constant domain neighbourhood semantics, we show that the systems NA^PR, MA^PR (written as NA^PR+(An)) and HA (written as NA^PR+(An)+(ECQ)) form a strictly increasing hierarchy of strength. Finally, we demonstrate the essential role of primitive recursive functions in weak arithmetic using classical countermodels.
tldr: The paper introduces a subminimal arithmetic system NA^PR with primitive recursive functions and characterizes the logical principles of Absorption of Negation and Ex Falso Quodlibet via arithmetical principles, establishing a strict hierarchy NA^PR ⊂ MA^PR ⊂ HA.
motivation: Negation's role in arithmetic is poorly understood at the substructural/subminimal level, and the authors want to isolate which arithmetical principles correspond to specific negation-related logical rules.
method: They define NA^PR (subminimal arithmetic with all primitive recursive functions), prove conservativity of Heyting Arithmetic over it for positive formulas, and use constant-domain neighbourhood semantics plus classical countermodels to compare deductive strength.
result: (ECQ) is shown equivalent to definability of disjunction and (An) to a variant of the least number principle; NA^PR, MA^PR and HA form a strictly increasing hierarchy, and primitive recursive functions are shown to be essential in weak arithmetic.
conclusion: Subminimal arithmetic provides a fine-grained framework for calibrating the arithmetical content of intuitionistic negation principles, clarifying interpretability relations between weak and full Heyting arithmetic.

title: LiHA: Worse Is Better For Lightweight Hash-based Source Authentication
authors: Negin Dehghanchaleshtori, Homit Dalia, Himanshu Chandra, Rohan Tripathi, Marc E. Fiuczynski, Richard P. Martin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The omission of source IP authentication remains a fundamental vulnerability in the Internet. Existing approaches rely on routing plausibility, topology assumptions, per-flow state, or wide deployment. These requirements have kept strong source authentication out of the data plane. As simplicity is the key to deployability, we present LiHA, a lightweight source authentication mechanism built around operations that routers already perform efficiently. LiHA binds secret keys to source prefixes using longest prefix match and authenticates each packet with a single message authentication code (MAC). The data plane requires no handshakes, per-flow state, or per-packet control plane access. A sender performs one prefix lookup and one fixed-size hash. The verifier repeats the same operations and forwards the packet only if the MAC matches. LiHA is designed for incremental deployment. It primarily protects against off-path attackers that spoof source prefixes they do not control. An on-path attacker can replay valid authenticated packets until the key rotates. LiHA does not eliminate every denial-of-service threat. Instead, it confines accepted traffic to authenticated source prefix space within participating networks. We argue that simpler source authentication with clear limits is more likely to be deployed. We implemented LiHA in three environments: as a set of user-space libraries, as eBPF programs, and in an FPGA. We found that the user-space implementation had very high overheads. The eBPF implementation got reasonable single thread performance even with a software based cryptographic hash. We found that only the FPGA could obtain 100 Gbps single thread performance, but that was only when bypassing the kernel using a DPDK user-level networking stack.
tldr: LiHA is a lightweight, incrementally deployable source-IP authentication scheme that binds secret keys to source prefixes via longest-prefix-match and authenticates packets with a single MAC, implemented in user-space, eBPF, and FPGA.
motivation: Source IP authentication has remained absent from the data plane because existing proposals require routing plausibility assumptions, per-flow state, or widespread deployment; the authors argue that a simpler mechanism with clearly stated limits is more likely to be adopted.
method: The sender performs one prefix lookup and one fixed-size hash to compute a MAC keyed by a secret bound to its source prefix; verifiers repeat the same operations and forward only on a MAC match, requiring no handshakes, per-flow state, or per-packet control-plane access, with implementations in user-space libraries, eBPF, and FPGA/DPDK.
result: User-space overhead was very high, eBPF achieved reasonable single-thread performance with a software hash, and only the FPGA with a DPDK kernel-bypass stack reached 100 Gbps single-thread throughput.
conclusion: LiHA confines accepted traffic to authenticated source-prefix space within participating networks and defends mainly against off-path spoofing, while on-path attackers can replay until key rotation; the authors position simplicity and explicit limitations as the path to deployment.

title: Closing The Applied Cybersecurity Gap In Critical Infrastructure: A Cyber-to-Physical Security Assessment Framework For Water Systems
authors: Kaan Sulkalar Halil Dursunoglu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of information technology and operational technology in water infrastructure creates pathways through which cyber compromise may affect physical service delivery. This study revisits the Applied Cybersecurity Gap (ACG) framework by evaluating an experimental Applied Cybersecurity Gap Index (ACGI) alongside the Cyber-to-Physical Propagation Rate (CPPR), defined as the proportion of initially compromised trials that produce a specified physical-impact outcome. The expanded evaluation comprises 2,160 synthetic trials across three water-network benchmarks, including EPANET Example Network 3 (Net3), and couples declared cyber-attack progression rules with hydraulic simulations. A source-trained machine-learning model evaluated on 247 compromised Net3 trials achieved ROC-AUC 0.772, PR-AUC 0.775, and F1 0.733, compared with 0.661, 0.642, and 0.704 for a scenario-only baseline. The configuration-cluster bootstrap interval for the ROC-AUC difference was 0.038--0.183. A separate 720-run Net3 hydraulic operating-point sensitivity analysis achieved the study's exploratory baseline pressure criterion in all reruns, preserved 717 of 720 physical-impact labels, and produced ROC-AUC 0.791 with the frozen source-trained model. Additional analyses examine the sensitivity of CPPR to the physical-impact threshold and assumed control-blocking probabilities, and demonstrate that the ACGI--CPPR association is partly induced by the simulation design rather than independently validated. The findings establish a reproducible simulation-based assessment workflow, but do not constitute field calibration of cybersecurity-control effectiveness or prediction of real-world utility incidents.
tldr: The paper proposes a simulation-based cyber-to-physical security assessment framework for water infrastructure, combining attack-progression rules with hydraulic simulation and a machine-learning model to predict physical-impact outcomes.
motivation: The convergence of IT and OT in water systems creates pathways for cyber compromise to disrupt physical service delivery, and existing security assessment approaches lack reproducible, quantitative methods for linking cyber attacks to physical consequences.
method: 2,160 synthetic trials across three water-network benchmarks (including EPANET Net3) couple declared cyber-attack progression rules with hydraulic simulations, using an Applied Cybersecurity Gap Index (ACGI) and a Cyber-to-Physical Propagation Rate (CPPR), plus a source-trained ML classifier and bootstrap sensitivity analyses.
result: The ML model reached ROC-AUC 0.772, PR-AUC 0.775, and F1 0.733 on 247 compromised Net3 trials versus a 0.661/0.642/0.704 baseline, with a bootstrap AUC-difference interval of 0.038–0.183; 717 of 720 physical-impact labels were preserved under hydraulic operating-point perturbations.
conclusion: The work establishes a reproducible simulation-based assessment workflow, but the ACGI–CPPR association is partly an artifact of simulation design and does not constitute field calibration or real-world incident prediction.

title: Efficient Cross-domain Multi-factor Authentication
authors: Yongjiao Li, Zhenlei Wang, Zhu Cao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Secure cross-domain authentication is crucial for protecting information exchange across terminals in different security domains. However, existing cross-domain authentication models suffer from inflexibility, high storage and computational consumption. In response to these problems, a cross-domain multi-factor authentication protocol with improved efficiency (CDAuth) is proposed. CDAuth employs a universally applicable multi-factor authentication approach, integrating pseudo-identity, attribute concealment, and biometric hiding. The authentication information sets can be freely added or modified to accommodate various access scenarios. This boosts privacy, flexibility, and applicability compared to traditional methods. Furthermore, multi-edge servers as Certification Authorities (CAs) store only the union of terminal attributes and a verification token per user in their subdomains, instead of each user's attribute and biometric sets as in traditional schemes, significantly reducing storage consumption. Additionally, replacing the bilinear pairing operations with the native group operations, while maintaining security, significantly reduces computational consumption. Our analysis shows that CDAuth can resist common security attacks and is more efficient than the previous schemes.
tldr: CDAuth is a classical cross-domain multi-factor authentication protocol that uses pseudo-identities, attribute concealment, and biometric hiding together with multi-edge-server CAs to cut storage and computation costs.
motivation: Existing cross-domain authentication schemes are inflexible and consume too much storage and computation, so the authors aim for a more efficient and flexible design.
method: The protocol combines pseudo-identity, attribute concealment, and biometric hiding in a modular attribute set that can be extended or modified, and replaces bilinear pairing operations with native group operations while distributing verification across multi-edge-server certification authorities.
result: The analysis shows that CDAuth resists common security attacks and is more efficient than prior schemes, with lower storage per user and reduced computational cost.
conclusion: CDAuth offers a practical, flexible, and efficient classical authentication solution for cross-domain environments, though it has no quantum or information-theoretic component.

title: BlindStep: A Secure One-Step Kernel For Privacy-Preserving Collaborative Reasoning
authors: Xiaoxian Liu, Xingyu Tan, Chen Chen, Xiaoyang Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A recurring step in two-party collaborative workflows combines a private candidate frontier with a partner's compatible evidence, scores the resulting candidates, and retains only a small frontier. Direct execution can expose intermediate candidates, local scores, or unauthorized evidence provenance. Existing MPC platforms and PSI protocols provide useful building blocks, but they do not define a unified post-alignment boundary for bounded-slot aggregation, fail-closed overflow handling, retained-frontier selection, and downstream disclosure. We present BlindStep, a fixed-shape MPC-online kernel for one such post-alignment step between two semi-honest parties. Given a frontend realizing the bounded-slot contract and an application enforcing the reveal policy [MATH], BlindStep provides a per-invocation simulation-based guarantee in the [MATH]-hybrid model: the kernel leaks only public setup parameters, fixed execution-shape metadata, a global overflow bit, and [MATH]-authorized Layer-2 disclosures. The guarantee excludes malicious security and multi-invocation composition, and treats frontend leakage and offline preprocessing separately. Within this kernel boundary, we implement six semi2k realizations in MP-SPDZ, crossing two sharing styles and three top-K strategies: H-variants compare over arithmetic shares, while B-variants convert packed ranking values to Boolean shares before selection.
