Under LAN, B-Queue is 6-7 times faster and uses about 40 times less communication than H-Queue at N = 256 and 2048. Against H-Sort on the same backend, B-Queue achieves speedups of 21 and 30 times and communication reductions of 204 and 290 times at N = 2048 and 8192, respectively. Under the evaluated N = 256, 100 ms RTT WAN profile, H-Sort becomes fastest, showing that round complexity can dominate backend choice for the measured MPC-online kernel.
tldr: BlindStep is a fixed-shape secure multi-party computation kernel that performs a bounded-slot top-K selection step between two semi-honest parties without leaking intermediate candidates or scores.
motivation: Two-party collaborative workflows that combine a private candidate frontier with a partner's evidence risk exposing intermediate candidates, local scores, and evidence provenance, and existing MPC platforms and PSI protocols do not define a unified post-alignment boundary for bounded-slot aggregation, fail-closed overflow, and retained-frontier selection.
method: The authors formalize a one-step post-alignment kernel in the arithmetic-sharing hybrid model with a simulation-based per-invocation guarantee, and implement six semi2k variants in MP-SPDZ spanning two sharing styles (arithmetic H-variants vs. Boolean-converted B-variants) and three top-K strategies.
result: Under LAN, B-Queue is 6-7x faster and uses ~40x less communication than H-Queue at N=256 and 2048, and beats H-Sort by 21-30x in time and 204-290x in communication at N=2048 and 8192; under a 100 ms RTT WAN profile H-Sort becomes fastest, showing round complexity can dominate.
conclusion: The kernel provides a well-defined leakage boundary for a single collaborative reasoning step, but explicitly excludes malicious security, multi-invocation composition, and treats frontend leakage and preprocessing separately.

title: Meshless Latent Dynamics Models For Model Order Reduction Of Time-dependent Partial Differential Equations
authors: Lorenzo Tomada, Federico Pichi, Gianluigi Rozza
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Latent dynamics learning has emerged as a prominent approach for Model Order Reduction (MOR) of time-dependent, parameterized Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). Traditional autoencoder-based approaches are intrinsically tied to fixed spatial discretizations during both training and inference, motivating the development of meshless methodologies. In this context, conditioning provides a natural mechanism for representing temporal evolution through spatially continuous functions, enabling mesh-agnostic Latent Dynamics Models (LDMs). In this work, we introduce a unified mathematical framework for mesh-agnostic LDMs based on conditioning in Neural Fields (NeFs). Leveraging a taxonomy of conditioning mechanisms (weak, strong, and pure), we formulate meshless LDMs as NeFs conditioned on a latent state. We establish a Universal Approximation Theorem (UAT) for this class of models and analyze their stability by deriving Lipschitz bounds for different conditioning mechanisms. Our analysis reveals an expressivity--stability trade-off, providing insight into why more expressive conditioning, despite its higher representational capacity, can potentially degrade performance during temporal extrapolation. Finally, we provide a comprehensive comparison of meshless and mesh-based architectures in the continuous limit of the spatial discretization, showing that meshless models guarantee grid-independent Lipschitz bounds, unlike mesh-based counterparts. Our experiments across Burgers' equation, Navier--Stokes flow past a cylinder, and linear advection show that meshless LDMs can achieve predictive accuracy comparable to or better than their mesh-based counterparts while using only 2% of the trainable parameters and exhibiting nearly constant error across spatial discretizations.
tldr: The paper introduces a unified framework for meshless latent dynamics models for model order reduction of time-dependent parameterized PDEs using conditioned neural fields.
motivation: Traditional autoencoder-based reduced-order models are tied to fixed spatial discretizations, motivating mesh-agnostic approaches for PDE surrogate modeling.
method: The authors formulate meshless latent dynamics models as neural fields conditioned on a latent state, classify conditioning mechanisms as weak, strong, or pure, prove a universal approximation theorem, and derive Lipschitz stability bounds.
result: Experiments on Burgers' equation, Navier-Stokes flow past a cylinder, and linear advection show predictive accuracy comparable to or better than mesh-based counterparts while using only 2% of the trainable parameters and achieving nearly constant error across spatial discretizations.
conclusion: Meshless latent dynamics models provide grid-independent Lipschitz bounds and an expressivity-stability trade-off, making them promising for discretization-agnostic PDE model order reduction.

title: Solyanik Estimates For Ergodic Flows
authors: Kesen Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a measure-preserving flow on a probability space [MATH] and let [MATH] be the associated one-sided ergodic maximal operator. We show that the sharp Tauberian constant [MATH],[MATH], equals [MATH] for every [MATH], unless every measurable set is invariant modulo null sets, in which case [MATH] for every [MATH]. In particular the Solyanik estimate [MATH] holds for every measure-preserving flow, and for ergodic flows on nonatomic spaces the estimate [MATH] holds with equality. This answers the one-parameter case of a question of Hagelstein and Parissis. The main point is the lower bound, which is obtained from a lacunary cross-section built out of the upcrossings of a probe function along the orbits of the flow.
tldr: This paper proves sharp Solyanik estimates for one-sided ergodic maximal operators associated with measure-preserving flows on probability spaces.
motivation: The work addresses the one-parameter case of a question by Hagelstein and Parissis concerning sharp Tauberian constants and Solyanik estimates in ergodic theory.
method: The author analyzes the ergodic maximal operator for measure-preserving flows and constructs a lacunary cross-section from upcrossings of a probe function along flow orbits to obtain the lower bound.
result: The sharp Tauberian constant is determined exactly for all flows, and the Solyanik estimate holds for every measure-preserving flow, with equality in the ergodic nonatomic case.
conclusion: The paper resolves the one-parameter flow version of the Hagelstein-Parissis question and establishes optimal ergodic maximal estimates.

title: Cyclic Nonassociative Bilinear Logic With Additive Constants As Extension Of Full Nonassociative Lambek Calculus
authors: Pawe{\l} P{\l}aczek (WSB Merito University In Poznan, Poland), Cheng-Syuan Wan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cyclic Linear Logic (CyMALL, CyBL) is a compromise between Commutative Linear Logic (MALL) and Noncommutative Linear Logic (Bilinear Logic, BL). We do not admit commutativity of the tensor, but we still admit only one De Morgan negation. MALL and its variants are natural extensions of Full Lambek Calculus (FL). Abrusci proved that CyBL is not a conservative extension of FL, if we admit additive constants in these logics. In this paper we show that Cyclic Nonassociative Bilinear Logic (CyNBL) with both additive constants is a strongly conservative extension of Full Nonassociative Lambek Calculus with only one additive constant - the upper bound - and that this holds even in the presence of an arbitrary set of nonlogical axioms.
tldr: The paper proves that cyclic nonassociative bilinear logic with both additive constants is a strongly conservative extension of full nonassociative Lambek calculus with only the upper additive constant.
motivation: Cyclic linear logics provide a middle ground between commutative and noncommutative linear logic, and conservativity questions are important for understanding their relationship to Lambek calculi.
method: The authors work in proof theory and algebraic logic, establishing strong conservativity even in the presence of arbitrary nonlogical axioms.
result: They show that CyNBL with both additive constants strongly conservatively extends Full Nonassociative Lambek Calculus with only one additive constant, the upper bound.
conclusion: This resolves a conservativity question for cyclic nonassociative bilinear logic and clarifies its relation to nonassociative Lambek calculus.

title: Evaluating Structural And Sat Attack Resilience In Cryptographic Dynamic Logic Locking Via Keystream Capping
authors: Nahush Tambe, Naseeruddin Lodge, Vineet Chadalavada, Fareena Saqib
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Untrusted third-party entities throughout the semiconductor supply chain expose proprietary hardware intellectual property to reverse engineering, piracy, and overproduction. While logic locking counters this threat by embedding key-dependent logic, conventional static key-gates remain vulnerable to both oracle-guided SAT attacks and structural removal attacks due to their time-invariant netlist signatures. Dynamic schemes such as STREAMLOCK mitigate oracle attacks by continuously masking signals with cryptographic keystream, achieving near 50\% Hamming distance output corruption under incorrect keys with low hardware overhead. However, confining key-gates to primary outputs leaves internal combinational cones vulnerable to single-tap structural bypasses. This work extends dynamic logic locking by distributing key-gates within internal paths prioritized via fault-propagation analysis. The original and internally-hardened architectures are evaluated against structural removal attacks and a bounded, unrolling-based SAT-style attack across three ISCAS'85 benchmarks. Distributing masking internally raises the uninformed attacker's brute-force search space from 6 candidate node subsets to over [MATH] for the largest benchmark. Crucially, empirical analysis reveals that topological relocation alone does not prevent algebraic key extraction when wide circuits expose numerous keystream bits per clock cycle. To eliminate this leak, a keystream-bit reuse cap is introduced to restrict per-cycle exposure independent of circuit width. Under this constraint, SAT-solver tractability encounters an immediate computational cliff, transitioning sharply from rapid under-constrained solving to timeout thresholds without disclosing the secret key. Integrating fault-aware internal placement with keystream reuse capping delivers joint resilience against structural bypasses and bounded SAT attacks.
tldr: The paper proposes an internally hardened dynamic logic-locking scheme with keystream-bit reuse capping to resist structural removal and bounded SAT-style attacks on hardware netlists.
motivation: Untrusted semiconductor supply chains expose hardware IP to reverse engineering and piracy, and existing dynamic logic locking can be bypassed by internal structural taps or algebraic key extraction in wide circuits.
method: The authors distribute key-gates along internal paths selected by fault-propagation analysis, then cap keystream-bit reuse per clock cycle to limit information exposure independent of circuit width, evaluating on ISCAS'85 benchmarks.
result: Internal masking increases attacker search space, and keystream capping causes SAT-solver tractability to drop sharply from under-constrained solving to timeout without revealing the key.
conclusion: Combining fault-aware internal key-gate placement with keystream reuse capping improves joint resilience against structural bypasses and bounded SAT attacks in classical hardware logic locking.

title: From Proof Of Concept To Practice: The Next Decade Of Artificial Intelligence In Metasurface Photonics
authors: Haoyue Jiang Sensong An
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over the past decade, artificial intelligence has learned to predict electromagnetic responses rapidly and generate high-performance metasurface designs. However, one question remains open: compared with conventional design workflows that contain no learned model, has it made the complete design workflow faster, and are the resulting devices better? We argue that the answer depends on the task. Reading 100 highly cited optical studies in depth, we distinguish the design tasks in which artificial intelligence is irreplaceable, clearly advantageous, or without clear advantage. In our view, the key to the next decade is not more successes in isolated tasks but making each success a foundation for the field, through shifts such as shared data, trained models, and physics written into learning. Whether artificial intelligence leaves lasting value in this field will depend on whether its benefits can be verified, its methods transferred, and its designs corrected by experiment.
tldr: A perspective reviewing 100 highly cited optical studies to assess whether AI genuinely accelerates and improves metasurface photonics design workflows relative to conventional methods.
motivation: Despite a decade of AI-driven electromagnetic response prediction and metasurface inverse design, it remains unclear whether learned models actually speed up the complete design pipeline or yield better devices than conventional workflows.
method: The authors perform a qualitative meta-analysis, reading 100 highly cited optical studies in depth and categorizing design tasks by whether AI is irreplaceable, clearly advantageous, or without clear advantage.
result: The benefit of AI is found to be task-dependent rather than universal, with clear gains in some inverse-design and response-prediction problems and no clear advantage in others.
conclusion: The field's next decade should focus on shared data, transferable trained models, and physics-informed learning so that individual successes become cumulative, experimentally verified, and reproducible foundations.

title: Understanding LLM-Based Bargaining Of Driving Agents In Mixed-Autonomy Traffic
authors: Lingxiao Zhou, Di Chen, Jia Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a flexible computational approach for modeling social interactions among heterogeneous agents. This paper develops a novel framework towards characterizing and understanding LLM-based population-level bargaining of shared road space between autonomous vehicle (AV) and human-driven vehicle (HV) agents in mixed-autonomy traffic. Through controlled experiments varying traffic density, agent objectives, and traffic-domain knowledge, we first characterize bargaining outcomes and observe heterogeneous agreement rates across different experimental conditions. To understand how the bargaining process shapes the outcomes, we introduce a behavioral taxonomy that jointly characterizes numerical bidding actions and communicative attitudes. We examine two complementary aspects of social interaction: inter-agent bargaining dynamics and private-to-public behavioral transformation. Results reveal distinct interaction patterns associated with agreement and breakdown, including greater constructive reciprocity in agreement trials and more frequent conflict escalation in breakdown trials. Furthermore, private and public communicative attitudes often differ even when numerical bids remain unchanged. These findings illustrate how LLM-based bargaining simulations can support a structured analysis of social interaction behaviors in mixed-autonomy traffic.
tldr: The paper builds an LLM-driven simulation framework to characterize how autonomous and human-driven vehicles bargain over shared road space in mixed-autonomy traffic.
motivation: LLMs offer a flexible way to model social interaction among heterogeneous agents, and mixed-autonomy traffic presents a setting where such bargaining behavior is poorly understood.
method: Controlled experiments vary traffic density, agent objectives, and traffic-domain knowledge, and a behavioral taxonomy jointly characterizes numerical bids and communicative attitudes across inter-agent bargaining and private-to-public transformation.
result: Agreement and breakdown trials show distinct patterns, with constructive reciprocity in agreements and conflict escalation in breakdowns, and private versus public attitudes often diverge even when bids stay fixed.
conclusion: LLM-based bargaining simulations can support structured analysis of social interaction in mixed-autonomy traffic.

title: Integration By Differentiation
authors: Alexandre M. Afonso
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we address a traditional pedagogical asymmetry between algorithmic differentiation and heuristic integration by introducing an extra parametric-order differential framework. By treating the order of differentiation as a parametric axis (discrete or continuous), classical integration is reframed as a local differential evaluation at the non-positive boundary level. This analytical shift alleviates some traditional routines of integration by parts, by replacing the quadrature of a product of elementary functions with a direct differential series that either truncates into a finite algebraic sum or resolves through cyclic symmetries. This parametric-order approach also bridges the gap with fractional calculus, showing that non-integer derivatives emerge as a seamless extension of the same operational dimension. By reducing global quadrature to local differentiation, this note offers an efficient, conceptual tool for undergraduate analysis.
tldr: The note introduces a parametric-order differential framework that reframes definite integration as a local differential evaluation at the zero-order boundary, streamlining integration by parts and connecting to fractional calculus.
motivation: There is a pedagogical asymmetry between algorithmic differentiation and heuristic integration, and the author aims to reduce global quadrature problems to local differentiation.
method: The order of differentiation is treated as a parametric axis (discrete or continuous), so integrals of products of elementary functions are computed via differential series that truncate finitely or close through cyclic symmetries.
result: The approach yields finite algebraic sums or cyclic resolution for standard integrals and shows non-integer derivatives arising naturally as an extension of the same operational dimension.
conclusion: The framework offers a conceptual and efficient tool for undergraduate analysis and provides a bridge to fractional calculus, though it is purely mathematical and pedagogical.

title: DistFlow And Its Conic Relaxation: Regularity, Monotonicity, And Hybrid Exactness Via Graph Decomposition
authors: Xinliang Dai
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical exactness conditions for conic relaxations of the DistFlow model rely, among other assumptions, either on all nodal injections being adjustable or on a network-wide path condition. In practice, these conditions may not hold uniformly across a feeder: controllable distributed energy resources (DERs) sit at some buses and fixed loads at others, while reverse flows from DER-rich regions can violate the path condition. This paper certifies exactness region by region and composes the regional certificates, accounting for perturbations that propagate downstream through voltages. We first introduce a subtree voltage stability region, in which the network and all compatible subtrees remain regular. Within it, two endpoint sign conditions, one relaxing the nonnegative-flow assumption and one implied by the classical path condition, yield monotone responses of voltages, currents, and losses to root voltages. Using duality, the implicit function theorem, and sign properties of inverse sensitivity matrices, we recast both classical arguments as individual sign certificates on branch multipliers. This turns exactness into a branchwise property that can be certified region by region. A partition rule then splits the network into dispatchable and passive subtrees, and a hybrid certificate combines their local conditions into exactness of the full-network relaxation, under additional operating-limit and objective conditions. In particular, placing controllable DERs at both ends of a branch with large reverse flow exempts that branch from the passive sign conditions.
tldr: The paper develops region-by-region exactness certificates for conic relaxations of the DistFlow model in power distribution networks, combining subtree voltage-stability regions, branchwise sign certificates on multipliers, and a graph-decomposition-based hybrid certificate.
motivation: Classical exactness conditions for DistFlow conic relaxations require either fully adjustable nodal injections or a network-wide path condition, which fail on realistic feeders with mixed controllable DERs and fixed loads plus reverse flows.
method: Introduces a subtree voltage stability region and two endpoint sign conditions, uses duality, the implicit function theorem, and sign properties of inverse sensitivity matrices to recast classical arguments as branchwise multiplier sign certificates, then partitions the network into dispatchable and passive subtrees to compose a hybrid exactness certificate.
result: Exactness becomes a branchwise property certifiable region by region, with a hybrid certificate combining local conditions into full-network exactness under additional operating-limit and objective conditions; branches with controllable DERs at both ends and large reverse flow are exempt from passive sign conditions.
conclusion: Regional certification plus graph decomposition yields broader and more practical exactness guarantees for DistFlow conic relaxations than network-wide classical conditions.

title: Stochastic Mirror Descent Under Dependent Observations
authors: Gersende Fort, Anatoli Juditsky, Jiaming Liang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the non-asymptotic convergence of Stochastic Mirror Descent (SMD) algorithm when the noisy first-order oracle is driven by dependent observations. Departing from the classical i.i.d. assumption underlying most existing guarantees, we introduce a flexible ``forgetting" condition that accommodates geometrically or polynomially dependent sequences. Under this condition we derive explicit finite-sample accuracy bounds for the averaged SMD iterates, recovering the classical [MATH] and [MATH] rates in the large- and small-initial-error regimes. We instantiate the general framework on two applications: high-dimensional linear regression with dependent regressors and nonparametric estimation of the drift function of a functional autoregressive model.
tldr: This paper derives finite-sample convergence bounds for Stochastic Mirror Descent when the stochastic oracle's noise is generated by dependent (geometrically or polynomially mixing) observations rather than i.i.d. samples.
motivation: Nearly all existing SMD convergence guarantees assume i.i.d. oracle noise, which fails in settings such as time-series regression or functional autoregressive models where observations are correlated.
method: The authors introduce a flexible 'forgetting' condition covering geometrically and polynomially dependent sequences, then establish explicit non-asymptotic accuracy bounds for averaged SMD iterates, and instantiate the framework on high-dimensional linear regression with dependent regressors and nonparametric drift estimation for a functional autoregressive model.
result: Explicit finite-sample bounds are obtained, recovering classical rates in both large- and small-initial-error regimes under the proposed dependence condition.
conclusion: SMD retains its favorable convergence behavior under dependent observations, extending its applicability to statistical learning problems with temporally correlated data.

title: Scaled-Gradient Hard Thresholding Algorithms For Sparse Signal Recovery
authors: Yun-Bin Zhao Nan Meng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thresholding methods provide a simple iterative framework for sparse signal recovery by combining a search direction with a thresholding operation. Gradient-based search directions are computationally efficient because they require only first-order information for the error metric. We incorporate componentwise gradient scaling into this framework by preserving large-magnitude components and attenuating the remaining components of the gradient of error metric. Combining this strategy with hard thresholding yields scaled-gradient hard thresholding (SGHT) and its pursuit variant SGHTP. Under suitable restricted isometry conditions, we establish recovery error bounds for both methods that account for measurement noise and deviations from exact sparsity. Numerical experiments indicate that SGHTP achieves recovery performance comparable to established pursuit methods on the tested ECG signals.
tldr: The paper introduces scaled-gradient hard thresholding (SGHT) and its pursuit variant SGHTP for sparse signal recovery, with recovery error bounds under restricted isometry conditions.
motivation: Thresholding methods offer a simple iterative framework for sparse recovery, and gradient-based search directions are cheap since they need only first-order error information; the authors aim to improve them by rescaling gradient components.
method: Componentwise gradient scaling is incorporated into the hard-thresholding framework, preserving large-magnitude gradient components while attenuating the rest, yielding SGHT and SGHTP; recovery error bounds accounting for measurement noise and sparsity deviation are derived under restricted isometry conditions.
result: Theoretical error bounds are established for both algorithms, and numerical experiments show SGHTP attains recovery performance comparable to established pursuit methods on tested ECG signals.
conclusion: Scaled-gradient hard thresholding provides a computationally efficient alternative for sparse signal recovery with competitive empirical performance, though the contribution lies entirely in classical compressive sensing.

title: Region-Preserving Accelerated Gradient Methods For Geodesically Convex Optimization
authors: Derun Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accelerated Riemannian optimization methods often require a priori assumptions that their iterates remain in a region where geometric bounds hold. We develop a parameterized inertial dynamical system and an explicit accelerated gradient method for smooth geodesically convex optimization on Riemannian manifolds with locally bounded sectional curvature. Our setting allows both positive and negative curvature without requiring completeness of the ambient manifold. Starting from a curvature-corrected continuous model, we construct the discrete updates by eliminating indefinite cross terms in the Lyapunov energy difference and derive verifiable conditions for a fixed step size. The resulting energy analysis establishes preservation of the initial geodesic ball without assuming iterate containment in advance. We further establish accelerated convergence rates for both geodesically convex and strongly geodesically convex objectives, without requiring restarts.
tldr: The paper develops a parameterized inertial dynamical system and an explicit accelerated gradient method for smooth geodesically convex optimization on Riemannian manifolds with locally bounded sectional curvature.
motivation: Accelerated Riemannian optimization methods typically assume a priori that iterates remain inside a region where geometric bounds hold, which is hard to verify; the authors aim to remove this assumption.
method: They start from a curvature-corrected continuous inertial model, then construct discrete updates by cancelling indefinite cross terms in the Lyapunov energy difference and derive verifiable fixed-step-size conditions.
result: The energy analysis proves preservation of the initial geodesic ball without assuming iterate containment in advance, and accelerated convergence rates are established for both geodesically convex and strongly geodesically convex objectives without restarts.
conclusion: The work provides a self-contained accelerated Riemannian gradient framework valid for both positive and negative curvature without manifold completeness, broadening the applicability of accelerated methods in geometric optimization.

title: Infeasible Momentum Orthogonalized Methods For Optimization On The Stiefel Manifold
authors: Yuxuan Zeng, Qi Deng, Dongdong Ge, Yinyu Ye
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study deterministic and stochastic optimization over the Stiefel manifold, explicitly allowing iterates to deviate from the manifold rather than enforcing feasibility via retraction at each step. We introduce Landom, a Landing-type method that constructs momentum in the relative-gradient direction, maps this update to its compact polar factor, and combines the resulting tangential step with a step along the negative gradient of the orthogonality penalty to improve feasibility. Under operator-to-nuclear smoothness, Landom achieves an [MATH] bound on the averaged nuclear norm of the relative gradient with exact gradients, and an [MATH] bound in expectation with stochastic momentum, bounded variance, and a fixed batch size. Our analysis also provides explicit pathwise bounds on the orthogonality residual, including its dependence on the step size and initial infeasibility. To address the coupling between objective and feasibility correction in Landom, we further propose Landom+, a two-timescale variant in which the tangential and normal step sizes are decoupled. By keeping the normal step size fixed, Landom+ achieves tighter control over the orthogonality residual following an initial transient while maintaining the respective convergence rates for stationarity. Numerical experiments across a range of applications illustrate that the proposed algorithms remain competitive with established manifold optimization approaches.
tldr: The paper introduces Landom and Landom+, infeasible (landing-type) momentum methods for deterministic and stochastic optimization over the Stiefel manifold that allow iterates to leave the manifold instead of retracting at every step.
motivation: Enforcing feasibility via retraction at each iteration is computationally costly in Riemannian/manifold optimization, so the authors seek methods that tolerate controlled infeasibility while still converging to stationary points.
method: Landom builds momentum in the relative-gradient direction, maps the update to its compact polar factor, and adds a normal step along the negative gradient of the orthogonality penalty; Landom+ decouples tangential and normal step sizes in a two-timescale scheme.
result: Under operator-to-nuclear smoothness the authors prove O(1/sqrt(T))-type bounds on the averaged nuclear norm of the relative gradient for exact and stochastic gradients, along with explicit pathwise bounds on the orthogonality residual depending on step size and initial infeasibility.
conclusion: The proposed infeasible momentum methods offer competitive empirical performance against established manifold-optimization approaches while providing convergence and feasibility guarantees.

title: PrivacyFlow: Privacy In Ai Agents Through Information Flow Analysis And Consequence-Aware Risk Management
authors: Robin Staab, Tom Wollschl\"ager, Vahab Mirrokni, Reza Shokri
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous LLM agents executing multi-step workflows over personal data often misalign with user privacy expectations and leak sensitive, out-of-context information. Although Contextual Integrity (CI) formalizes this problem, existing benchmarks and defenses rarely operationalize CI for realistic multi-step task sequences in evolving environments. In this work, we first introduce agentic PrivacyBench, a benchmark of 5873 tasks in 986 task sequences with dynamic environment updates and CI-grounded allow-sets for sensitive information. We also introduce PrivacyFlow, a defense that separates deliberative privacy planning (System 2) from task execution (System 1), treating each sharing decision as a structured risk-management problem. Before execution, PrivacyFlow traces the provenance and purpose of each planned data flow, models recipient background knowledge, and simulates what external actors could infer. This allows us to model the downstream consequences of disclosure, including inference attacks and context-dependent harms. It then weighs the remaining disclosure risk against task utility and executes a minimized plan, blocks it, or consults the user. Across six models, PrivacyFlow significantly reduces step-level privacy failures and raises the share of completed task sequences without a detected privacy violation by 22--55 percentage points. We further highlight a new privacy--utility--autonomy tradeoff: allowing PrivacyFlow to proactively prompt the user in case of uncertainty can increase authorized task completion at the cost of shifting decision effort back to the user. Our results suggest that proactive CI reasoning can substantially improve agentic privacy and motivate further study of this tradeoff.
tldr: PrivacyFlow is a defense framework for autonomous LLM agents that separates privacy planning from task execution, tracing data provenance and modeling downstream inference risks to minimize disclosure under Contextual Integrity.
motivation: Multi-step LLM agents operating over personal data can leak out-of-context sensitive information, and existing benchmarks and defenses rarely operationalize Contextual Integrity for realistic evolving multi-step workflows.
method: The authors build agentic PrivacyBench (5873 tasks across 986 sequences with dynamic environment updates and CI-grounded allow-sets), and propose PrivacyFlow, a System 2 / System 1 split that treats each sharing decision as a risk-management problem by tracing provenance and purpose, modeling recipient background knowledge, and simulating what external actors could infer.
result: Across six models, PrivacyFlow substantially reduces step-level privacy failures and increases the fraction of task sequences completed without a detected violation by 22-55 percentage points, while revealing a privacy-utility-autonomy tradeoff when the system proactively queries the user.
conclusion: Proactive Contextual-Integrity reasoning can materially improve agentic privacy, motivating further study of the tradeoff between privacy, task utility, and user decision burden.

title: Renegotiable Options Fail To Prevent Hold-Up Between Two Profit-Maximizing Frontier Llm Agents
authors: Junwei Yao, Zike Yang, Yongxi Zhou, Yanxian Chen, Jianan Liu, Jiaxi Wen, Zhijun Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Do contract terms that protect investment between people also protect it between profit-maximizing language-model agents? In the hold-up problem, a seller can adapt a unit to one buyer at a cost before the price is set. Once that cost is sunk, the buyer can offer almost nothing and the seller will still accept, so a seller who foresees this does not adapt. One remedy is an option: the buyer may buy at a fixed price. In theory the option stops working if the buyer can let it lapse and offer its own price instead. Yet in a laboratory experiment by Hoppe and Schmitz, this renegotiable option raised human investment from 41.5% of pairs without a contract to 67.2%. We had Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, each told to maximize its side's profit, play a one-shot game with the same strategic structure under their four contract regimes and a reference-price control. The agents did what game theory predicts: under the renegotiable option no seller adapted, and under the option that rules out this renegotiation every seller did. In a second experiment in which sellers no longer stated their expected revenue before deciding, removing the profit instruction left investment unchanged under no contract and both options. When we changed the numbers so that the buyer would exercise the option even without adaptation, adapting only added cost, and no seller adapted: the agents did not simply adapt whenever an option was offered or whenever its price covered the cost. Under our protocol, a contract term that raised investment between people did not protect it between agents.
tldr: Two frontier LLM agents (Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol) play a one-shot hold-up game under four contract regimes, and unlike humans they fail to use renegotiable options to sustain investment.
motivation: The authors ask whether contractual remedies that mitigate hold-up between humans also work between profit-maximizing language-model agents, a question relevant to AI-agent economics and mechanism design.
method: Behavioral game-theoretic experiment: each agent, instructed to maximize its side's profit, plays a one-shot hold-up game with a seller-adaptation stage and buyer pricing stage under no contract, a renegotiable option, a non-renegotiable option, and controls, with additional variations removing revenue statements, profit instructions, and altering payoffs.
result: Agents behaved as game theory predicts: no seller adapted under the renegotiable option, while every seller adapted under the non-renegotiable option; removing the profit instruction did not change investment, and agents did not adapt merely because an option was offered or its price covered costs.
conclusion: Under this protocol, a contract term that raised human investment (41.5% to 67.2%) failed to protect investment between profit-maximizing LLM agents, suggesting limits to transferring human-tested institutional remedies to AI agents.

title: When Safety Checks Become Privacy Risks: A Privacy-Preserving Paradigm For Llm Agent Safety Auditing
authors: Yixiang Luo, Ziheng Ma, Ke Chang, Jian Wang, Jiqiang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents interact with online services through tool calls that may access private data or perform sensitive actions. Specialized providers can supply and maintain pre-execution safety auditing capabilities for agent operators. However, sending task descriptions, call arguments, and interaction histories to an external auditor may expose sensitive user information. In this work, we propose a paradigm for privacy-preserving safety auditing that separates delegated audit computation from plaintext access and execution authority. Grounded in a three-domain auditing model, the paradigm connects trusted representation construction, encrypted audit computation, and trusted decision and execution through explicit interfaces. These interfaces accommodate alternative representations and scorers, while encrypted computation protects audit inputs from a semi-honest auditor. We instantiate this paradigm in SealCall, a framework combining learned audit representations, CKKS-based encrypted similarity computation, and execution control bound to audited tool calls. Evaluated on 1,252 public binary candidates, SealCall achieves a mean F1 score of 0.840 under grouped nested evaluation, while preserving plaintext audit decisions in all measured cases. A representative configuration completes each encrypted scoring operation in 0.176 s.
tldr: The paper proposes a privacy-preserving paradigm, instantiated as SealCall, for auditing the safety of LLM agent tool calls using CKKS homomorphic encryption so that an external auditor never sees plaintext task data.
motivation: LLM agents invoke tools that touch private data, and outsourcing pre-execution safety auditing to specialized providers risks exposing sensitive task descriptions, arguments, and interaction histories.
method: The authors define a three-domain auditing model that connects trusted representation construction, encrypted audit computation, and trusted decision/execution through explicit interfaces, then implement it with learned audit representations, CKKS-based encrypted similarity scoring, and execution control tied to audited calls.
result: On 1,252 public binary candidates under grouped nested evaluation, SealCall reaches a mean F1 of 0.840 while preserving plaintext audit decisions in all measured cases, with each encrypted scoring operation taking 0.176 s in a representative configuration.
conclusion: Encrypted audit computation can support practical LLM agent safety auditing without granting the auditor plaintext access, though the work is a classical privacy/security engineering contribution.

title: CuPIQP: A Batched And Differentiable Qp Solver On GPUs For Robot Learning And Control
authors: Fenglong Song, Roland Schwan, Yuwen Chen, Yuning Jiang, Colin N. Jones
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quadratic programs (QPs) are fundamental building blocks of many robotic tasks such as inverse kinematics, whole-body control, and model predictive control. Extending these methods to large-scale robot learning and control requires solving many QPs concurrently and, for end-to-end learning, differentiating through their solutions. Efficient batched optimization is therefore essential to bringing established model-based methods into GPU-based robotics pipelines. We present , a batched and differentiable QP solver on GPUs based on a proximal interior-point method, with unified support for dense, sparse, and multistage problems. The solver exploits parallelism across independent QPs and their internal structure while preserving per-problem numerical updates and termination decisions. Benchmarks with up to 16384 QPs per batch demonstrate solve-time speedups of up to [MATH] over and [MATH] over eight-core . In an end-to-end learning task, accelerates training by [MATH] over and [MATH] over . By reducing the computational cost, provides efficient, reusable infrastructure for integrating model-based optimization into large-scale robot learning and control.
tldr: CuPIQP is a batched, differentiable GPU quadratic-program solver built on a proximal interior-point method for robot learning and control.
motivation: Model-based robotic tasks such as inverse kinematics, whole-body control, and MPC require solving many QPs concurrently and differentiating through their solutions, which is expensive on CPU pipelines.
method: The authors implement a proximal interior-point QP solver on GPUs with unified support for dense, sparse, and multistage problems, exploiting parallelism across independent QPs while keeping per-problem numerical updates and termination decisions.
result: Batches of up to 16384 QPs show solve-time speedups over competing solvers and eight-core CPU baselines, and end-to-end learning experiments show substantial training acceleration.
conclusion: The solver provides reusable, efficient infrastructure for embedding model-based optimization into large-scale GPU robotics pipelines.

title: Angler: Verifier-Grounded Benchmarking With An Adaptive Attacker For Web Agents
authors: Yini Huang, Aiwen LU, Zhen Sun, Yi Han, Yuzhi Zhao, Jiaheng Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents are increasingly deployed to complete tasks autonomously on real websites, where adversarially injected content can induce them to perform unauthorized actions. Existing evaluations primarily use fixed attacks or focus on a single attack type, and evaluate attacks at the text level rather than through real state changes, thus underestimating how vulnerable agents are to diverse attacks. To address the gap, we introduce REEF, a benchmark of red-teaming executable environments with faithful verification for measuring the security vulnerabilities of web agents. REEF covers 9 verifier-grounded websites spanning travel, commerce, productivity, media, and communication, and pairs every authentic benign task with a malicious objective delivered through 5 attack types at both the user and the environment level. REEF's state-based verifiers provide the execution feedback that drives ANGLER, an adaptive near-miss-guided lure evolution framework for red-teaming. Rather than evaluating a fixed attack set, ANGLER uses outcomes from prior rollouts to guide LLM-based attack mutation and candidate selection, prioritizing near-miss seeds during refinement. Across 8 VLM-based web agents, ANGLER achieves an end-to-end attack success rate (ASR) of 20.36%, compared with 15.24% for the non-adaptive setting. Compared with attack-free execution on the same benign tasks, attacks generated by ANGLER reduce benign task success rate (BSR) from 61.9% to 44.4%.
tldr: The paper introduces REEF, a verifier-grounded red-teaming benchmark of executable web environments, together with ANGLER, an adaptive near-miss-guided attack-mutation framework for measuring the security vulnerabilities of VLM-based web agents.
motivation: Web agents deployed on real websites can be manipulated by adversarially injected content, but existing evaluations use fixed attacks, cover only a single attack type, and judge success at the text level instead of via real state changes, thereby underestimating vulnerability.
method: REEF comprises 9 verifier-grounded websites across travel, commerce, productivity, media and communication, pairing each benign task with malicious objectives delivered through 5 attack types at user and environment level; state-based verifiers supply execution feedback that drives ANGLER's LLM-based mutation and near-miss-prioritized candidate selection.
result: Across 8 VLM-based web agents, ANGLER attains a 20.36% end-to-end attack success rate versus 15.24% for non-adaptive attacks, and reduces benign task success rate from 61.9% to 44.4% relative to attack-free execution.
conclusion: Adaptive, verifier-grounded red-teaming exposes substantially greater vulnerability in web agents than fixed attack sets, motivating execution-level security benchmarks for agentic systems.

title: Pareto-Optimal Hypersonic Vehicle Design With Canonical-Coordinate Neural Operator Surrogates Under Ablation-Driven Shape Change And Incidence Variation
authors: Khemraj Shukla, Jeremy Redding, Luis Bravo, George Em Karniadakis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-fidelity CFD is essential for coupled hypersonic aerodynamic and aerothermal phenomena, but its cost precludes multi-objective design optimization. We develop three DeepONet surrogates for two hypersonic configurations, unified by one device: the trunk receives coordinates in which the varying feature is held fixed. The first is a prescribed family of 37 spherically blunted tangent ogives, varied through ogive radius of curvature to span nose-tip ablation forebody change; no ablation is computed. A body-fitted canonical transformation maps every domain onto a common (s, eta) space, retaining physical coordinates for forces and heat transfer. A branch network predicts reduced coefficients and a Transolver trunk with Physics-Attention learns the spatial basis; a two-step strategy optimizes both jointly, orthonormalizes the basis by QR factorization, and trains a second-stage branch for unseen geometries. Surrogates cover density, pressure, velocity, temperatures, conductivities and species mass fractions. In leave-one-out tests, drag, mean and peak wall heat flux are recovered to 1.16%, 1.62% and 5.29%; a sweep of 1001 geometries gives a 200-design Pareto front trading 6.68% in drag for 4.42% in peak heating (a diagnostic, not an objective). The second is the 3D AEDC waverider at 29 angles of attack: static mesh, moving leading-edge shock. For surface quantities, the same construction predicts integrated heat load within 0.22% and force coefficients to errors below 2.6x10^-5; Pareto fronts identify angles of attack trading drag, lift and heating. For the volume field, a Cartesian trunk smears the shock; a frozen ShockNet supplies a shock-aligned coordinate and a hotspot-aware mixture of experts corrects the residual, recovering density to 12.28% relative L2 error at a held-out incidence (5.08x10^7 nodes). The 1001-design sweep takes about three minutes on a single CPU.
tldr: The authors build three DeepONet-based neural-operator surrogates for hypersonic aerodynamics and aerothermal fields, using canonical coordinate transformations to handle ablation-driven shape change and incidence variation, and use them for Pareto-optimal vehicle design.
motivation: High-fidelity CFD for coupled hypersonic aerodynamic and aerothermal phenomena is too expensive for multi-objective design optimization, so fast yet accurate surrogates are needed to explore large design spaces.
method: A body-fitted canonical transformation maps each geometry to a common (s, eta) space with the varying feature held fixed in the trunk input; a branch network predicts reduced coefficients and a Transolver trunk with Physics-Attention learns the spatial basis, trained in a two-step joint scheme with QR orthonormalization, plus a frozen ShockNet and mixture-of-experts correction for volumetric shock fields.
result: Leave-one-out tests recover drag, mean and peak wall heat flux to 1.16%, 1.62% and 5.29%; surface heat load on the AEDC waverider is predicted within 0.22% and volume density to 12.28% relative L2 error, while a 1001-design sweep runs in about three minutes on a single CPU.
conclusion: Canonical-coordinate neural-operator surrogates enable practical many-query Pareto optimization of hypersonic vehicles under shape change and incidence variation, though the resulting fronts are diagnostic rather than definitive design objectives.

title: Terminal-state Theorems For A Two-stage Maki--Thompson Rumor Model: Final Size, Stifler Composition, And Non-identifiability From Pooled Statistics
authors: Qingquan Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rumor models of the Daley--Kendall and Maki--Thompson family anchor the statistical mechanics of social contagion, yet the stifler composition a rumor leaves behind has resisted closed-form analysis. Inspired by the asymmetric two-step pairing (A2SP) process of step-growth polymerization, we import its common-factor cancellation into a minimal two-stage MT variant in which re-contacted spreaders are re-activated into a senior class at rate [MATH] rather than stifled, and obtain exact terminal-state theorems. (i) Saturation: the rumor exhausts the ignorant pool for every stifling-to-recruitment ratio [MATH], with a three-way tail classification and a logarithmically critical line at [MATH]. (ii) Final size: the terminal stifler pool splits as [MATH], independent of seed size; the fingerprint inverts linearly ([MATH]) and matches Gillespie simulations within [MATH]. (iii) Pooled versus history-resolved: pooled statistics are exactly [MATH]-free on any static graph; only the history-resolved composition carries [MATH]. Restoring the classic teller-retires channel breaks the exact closure beyond quantified gates (contact rates of [MATH]--[MATH] of [MATH] for spreader channels at [MATH], up to [MATH] at [MATH]), and on configuration-model networks the composition bias decays as [MATH]. An exploratory inversion of 354,930 Higgs--Twitter retweet episodes, screened by an identity check and four negative controls, yields [MATH] (joint cluster-bootstrap CI [MATH]; [MATH] after calibration at the matched threshold). Terminal compositions identify this effective re-activation rate, an upper bound on contact-coupled re-activation; the mechanism itself requires timing information beyond the terminal state.
tldr: This paper develops exact terminal-state theorems for a two-stage Maki-Thompson rumor spreading model inspired by step-growth polymerization, analyzing final stifler composition and identifiability from pooled statistics.
motivation: Rumor models in the Daley-Kendall and Maki-Thompson family are important for social contagion dynamics, but the final composition of stiflers has lacked closed-form analysis.
method: The authors import a common-factor cancellation from an asymmetric two-step pairing process into a minimal two-stage Maki-Thompson variant where re-contacted spreaders are re-activated rather than stifled, deriving exact terminal-state results and testing them with Gillespie simulations and Twitter retweet data.
result: They obtain saturation classification, a linear final-size fingerprint independent of seed size, and show pooled statistics are free of the re-activation parameter on static graphs while history-resolved composition carries it; empirical inversion yields an effective re-activation rate with confidence intervals.
conclusion: Terminal compositions can identify an effective re-activation rate, but the underlying mechanism requires timing information beyond terminal-state statistics.

title: Adversarial Wronskians: A Proof Of The Kung--Traub Conjecture
authors: Matthew J. Colbrook
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Kung--Traub conjecture: a deterministic stationary root-finding method without memory, using at most [MATH] real scalar function or derivative evaluations per iteration, cannot have local order greater than [MATH] on every real analytic function with a simple zero. For [MATH], the bound is attained by the methods of Kung and Traub. The local estimate is required at every sufficiently close starting point, with constants that may depend on the function. Evaluation points and derivative orders may be chosen adaptively, and the rules for choosing them and processing the data are unrestricted. The proof uses a localisation property of polynomial Wronskians to obtain a lower bound at each fixed scale. A diagonal construction then gives one entire function, with derivative bounded above and below on the real line, for which every larger order fails. We also obtain a sharper bound when evaluations are made in prescribed groups, and prove the corresponding result for complex scalar evaluations. The results of this paper are also formally verified in Lean.
tldr: The paper proves the Kung–Traub conjecture, establishing that memoryless deterministic root-finding methods using at most n evaluations per iteration cannot exceed order 2^(n-1) for real analytic functions with simple zeros.
motivation: The Kung–Traub conjecture has been a long-standing open problem in numerical analysis bounding the convergence order of multipoint iterative root-finding schemes without memory.
method: The proof exploits a localization property of polynomial Wronskians to derive a lower bound at each fixed scale, combined with a diagonal construction producing a single entire function with bounded derivatives on the real line that defeats any higher-order method; the results are also formalized in Lean.
result: The conjecture is proven for real scalar evaluations, with a sharper bound obtained when evaluations occur in prescribed groups, and the corresponding complex-scalar result is established.
conclusion: The work settles a classical conjecture in computational mathematics and provides formally verified proofs, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Point-to-ellipse Series -- Part Ii Expansion About The Center
authors: John-Olof Nilsson
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Power series expansions in the polar distance about the center are derived for the normal direction and signed distance from an ellipse to points near its center. After extracting constant terms and common factors, the series coefficients are polynomials in the axis ratio and the absolute value of the sine of the polar angle, with rational coefficients. The region of convergence is shown to be the region bounded by the ellipse evolute. The expansions complement previously derived expansions valid for points far from the center.
tldr: This paper derives power series expansions in the polar distance about the center for the normal direction and signed distance from an ellipse, with convergence bounded by the ellipse evolute.
motivation: The authors aim to complement previously derived expansions that are valid for points far from the ellipse center, completing a 'point-to-ellipse' series of results.
method: Analytic derivation of power series in polar distance about the center, extracting constant terms and common factors to express coefficients as polynomials in axis ratio and |sin(polar angle)| with rational coefficients, plus convergence analysis.
result: Series coefficients are shown to be polynomials in the axis ratio and the absolute sine of the polar angle with rational coefficients, and the region of convergence is proven to be the region bounded by the ellipse evolute.
conclusion: The new expansions complement earlier far-from-center expansions, giving a complete series description of normal direction and signed distance to an ellipse.

title: On Some Special Cases Of The Weber-Schafheitlin Integral
authors: V. G. Zborovskii
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider special cases of the discontinuous Weber--Schafheitlin integral in which the orders [MATH] and [MATH] of the Bessel functions differ by an integer and the exponent [MATH] equals [MATH] or [MATH], with [MATH] odd. Explicit closed-form results are obtained in terms of Jacobi polynomials.
tldr: The paper derives closed-form expressions for special cases of the discontinuous Weber-Schafheitlin integral involving Bessel functions whose orders differ by an integer, expressed via Jacobi polynomials.
motivation: The Weber-Schafheitlin integral is a classical object in the theory of special functions, and certain discontinuous parameter regimes with integer order differences and odd exponents lack explicit evaluations.
method: Analytic derivation of the integral for the cases where the Bessel function orders differ by an integer and the exponent equals a specific value with odd parameter, using known properties of Bessel functions and orthogonal polynomials.
result: Explicit closed-form results are obtained, written in terms of Jacobi polynomials for the considered parameter regimes.
conclusion: The work extends the tabulated theory of Weber-Schafheitlin integrals and provides compact polynomial-form evaluations useful for further analytic work in special function theory.

title: Equivariant Gradient Degree Comparison Via Clarke Duality For Strongly Indefinite Hamiltonian Systems
authors: Shi Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study equivariant gradient degree comparisons for strongly indefinite Hamiltonian systems through Clarke duality. Under suitable convexity and compactness assumptions, we establish a correspondence between the primal and dual equations that preserves the symmetries of their solutions. We derive an identity relating their negative spectral representations and show that the Galerkin-normalized local index of the primal linearization coincides with the equivariant gradient degree determined by the dual Hessian. This comparison extends to infinite-dimensional settings through stabilized Galerkin approximations. We also establish relations between primal and dual crossing forms, equivariant spectral flow, and local equivariant gradient degrees at nondegenerate fixed solutions. The results provide a framework for studying equivariant bifurcation in strongly indefinite systems. As an application, we consider periodic Hamiltonian ring equations with dihedral symmetry and illustrate the computation of equivariant gradient degrees and bifurcation invariants.
tldr: A pure-mathematics paper developing equivariant gradient degree comparisons for strongly indefinite Hamiltonian systems via Clarke duality, with applications to bifurcation in dihedrally symmetric Hamiltonian ring equations.
motivation: The authors aim to connect primal and dual variational formulations of strongly indefinite Hamiltonian systems in a symmetry-preserving way, extending classical degree-theoretic tools to infinite-dimensional equivariant settings.
method: Using Clarke duality under convexity and compactness assumptions, they relate primal and dual equations, derive identities between negative spectral representations, and extend results to infinite dimensions through stabilized Galerkin approximations, also connecting crossing forms and equivariant spectral flow.
result: They show that the Galerkin-normalized local index of the primal linearization coincides with the equivariant gradient degree determined by the dual Hessian, and establish relations among primal/dual crossing forms at nondegenerate fixed solutions.
conclusion: The framework provides tools for studying equivariant bifurcation in strongly indefinite systems, illustrated on periodic Hamiltonian ring equations with dihedral symmetry.

title: Scientist Mothers Working In Childcare Deserts Are Less Likely To Attain Tenure
authors: Jun Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.40951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Childcare shortages have limited families' access to quality care, with consequences for children's development and parents' careers. We link two decades of childcare supply data to longitudinal surveys of U.S. scientists. We find workplace childcare deserts are widespread: more than half of scientists at universities and research institutions work in deserts, where supply falls significantly short of demand. We further find mothers working in deserts are less likely to attain tenure. They are also more likely to move to industry and part-time positions. Reduced work time partly accounts for the tenure association but other reasons remain. Expanding childcare availability near workplaces may help retain scientific talent.
tldr: A science-policy study linking two decades of U.S. childcare supply data to longitudinal scientist surveys shows that mothers working in childcare deserts are less likely to earn tenure.
motivation: Childcare shortages constrain families' access to quality care, potentially harming children's development and parents' academic careers, yet the link between local childcare supply and scientists' career outcomes had not been quantified.
method: The authors combine two decades of geo-coded childcare supply data with longitudinal surveys of U.S. scientists to identify workplace childcare deserts and estimate associations with tenure attainment and career trajectories, including mediation by reduced work hours.
result: Over half of scientists at universities and research institutions work in childcare deserts; mothers in these deserts are less likely to attain tenure and more likely to move to industry or part-time positions, with reduced work time only partly explaining the tenure gap.
conclusion: Expanding childcare availability near workplaces may help retain scientific talent, particularly mothers, and mitigate gendered attrition from academic research careers.

title: String-averaging Bargaining In Solidarity Cooperative Games
authors: Soumitra Dey Yair Censor
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the situation that the grand set of all players, in a cooperative game in characteristic function form with a nonempty core, consists of recognizable subsets of players. The underlying assumption is that the players of each subset have something in common between themselves which is not shared by the players of other subsets. For example, the members of these subsets are distinguishable by their nationalities or by their geographic locations or by some other market-related economic or social property. In addition to the agreement of all players to play the game to reach a point in the core, the members of each subset want to steer the iterative orbit of the bargaining process to a point in the core that will reflect the strength of their solidarity within their subset. This is why we call such subsets solidarity sets. The solidarity means that players of a solidarity set are willing to participate in coalitions that include only members of their solidarity set and are not willing to participate in coalitions of other solidarity sets. The question is how can such a game be played? Is there an iterative bargaining scheme that will generate a sequence of payoffs that converges to a point in the core which reflects the solidarity of the members of the solidarity sets? We propose bargaining schemes that allow the members of each solidarity set to perform, independently from other solidarity sets and, therefore, simultaneously in time, a full but finite sweep of intercoalitional collaboration. Then the end-points of all these sweeps are combined into a single payoff vector via a convex combination wherein the coefficients of the convex combination may reflect some a priori knowledge about the relative strengths of the different solidarity sets. These bargaining schemes are applied to a new type of cooperative game that we call solidarity cooperative game (SCG).
tldr: The paper introduces 'solidarity cooperative games', a cooperative game-theoretic framework in which recognizable subsets of players bargain iteratively to reach a core payoff vector reflecting intra-subset solidarity.
motivation: Classical cooperative game bargaining schemes ignore the fact that players often form distinguishable groups (nationality, geography, economic or social ties) whose members refuse coalitions outside their group, so a new formalism is needed to model such solidarity-constrained bargaining toward the core.
method: Each solidarity set independently performs a finite sweep of intercoalitional collaboration; the resulting sweep end-points are merged into a single payoff vector via a convex combination whose coefficients encode a priori relative strengths of the sets, yielding an iterative string-averaging-type bargaining scheme.
result: The proposed bargaining schemes generate payoff sequences that converge to a point in the core of the game, with the limit point reflecting the relative solidarity strengths encoded in the convex combination coefficients.
conclusion: Solidarity cooperative games and the associated string-averaging bargaining schemes provide a principled way to play core-reaching cooperative games under group-solidarity constraints, opening a new class of game-theoretic problems.

title: Robust Edge Multiscale Space Based Hybrid Schwarz Preconditioner For High-frequency Helmholtz Problems
authors: Shubin Fu, Shihua Gong, Guanglian Li, Yulei Liao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a novel hybrid Schwarz method, termed the robust edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz method (REMs-HS), for the efficient solution of high-frequency Helmholtz problems. The method combines a one-level restricted additive Schwarz preconditioner with impedance transmission conditions (RAS-imp) and an edge multiscale (EMs) coarse solver in a multiplicative way. A key ingredient of our construction is a modified impedance boundary condition (mIBC), which is imposed both on the subdomain problems and on the local problems that generate the EMs coarse space. Compared with the original impedance boundary condition, the mIBC makes the proposed method both stable and inexpensive theoretically. We prove that the resulting REMs-HS preconditioner gives rise to a uniform convergent fixed-point iteration for large wavenumbers. Moreover, the required resolution conditions are substantially relaxed. Only a mild condition on the level parameter [MATH] of the hierarchical coarse basis [MATH] is needed, which is markedly weaker than the conditions in previous analyses. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method for Helmholtz problems with large wavenumbers.
tldr: The authors propose a robust edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz preconditioner (REMs-HS) for efficiently solving high-frequency Helmholtz problems.
motivation: High-frequency Helmholtz problems are notoriously difficult to solve iteratively because of the indefinite, highly oscillatory nature of the operator, and existing domain decomposition methods require restrictive resolution conditions.
method: The method multiplicatively combines a one-level restricted additive Schwarz preconditioner with impedance transmission conditions (RAS-imp) and an edge multiscale (EMs) coarse solver, using a modified impedance boundary condition (mIBC) on both subdomain and coarse-space local problems.
result: The authors prove uniform convergence of the resulting fixed-point iteration for large wavenumbers under substantially relaxed resolution conditions, requiring only a mild condition on the coarse level parameter, and confirm robustness numerically.
conclusion: REMs-HS offers a stable and inexpensive preconditioner for high-frequency Helmholtz problems, with weaker theoretical requirements than prior analyses and demonstrated numerical robustness.

title: Turnpike Properties For Exploratory Stochastic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control With Indefinite Cost Functionals
authors: Yaohua Hu, Zhaoqing Li, Hanxiao Wang, Jie Xiong
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous-time exploratory stochastic control provides a stochastic control framework for the exploration--exploitation trade-off in reinforcement learning. In this paper, we study the long-time behavior of finite-horizon exploratory stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) optimal control problems as the time horizon [MATH], and establish so-called turnpike properties for such problems. In the finite-horizon setting, we derive a feedback representation of the exploratory stochastic LQ problem and analyze its long-time structure. We formulate an exploratory static distribution optimization problem analogous to the classical static optimization problem and identify the corresponding static reference object. We prove a turnpike property for the optimal state process relative to a stochastic reference process, as well as a Wasserstein turnpike property for the optimal control distribution. In addition to the exploratory control formulation, another key feature of our results is that, by introducing a joint coercivity condition, we allow the cost functional to be indefinite and the controlled state system to be merely stabilizable. Consequently, the derived turnpike property is novel even within the classical stochastic LQ control framework.
tldr: The paper establishes turnpike properties for finite-horizon exploratory stochastic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with indefinite cost functionals as the horizon grows large.
motivation: Exploratory stochastic control formalizes the exploration-exploitation trade-off in reinforcement learning, and understanding the long-time (horizon-asymptotic) structure of such problems is needed to characterize their limiting behavior.
method: The authors derive a feedback representation of the exploratory stochastic LQ problem, formulate an exploratory static distribution optimization problem with a corresponding static reference object, and prove a turnpike property for the optimal state process together with a Wasserstein turnpike property for the optimal control distribution, using a joint coercivity condition that allows indefinite costs and merely stabilizable dynamics.
result: Turnpike convergence of the optimal state towards a stochastic reference process and Wasserstein convergence of the control distributions are proven; the results are new even in the classical stochastic LQ framework.
conclusion: The work extends turnpike theory to exploratory stochastic control under weakened coercivity and stabilizability assumptions, providing new structural insight for RL-motivated control problems.

title: Koopman--Lyapunov And Koopman--Riccati Controller Synthesis
authors: Wentao Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While the Koopman operator-based lifted representations of nonlinear autonomous and controlled systems have been well covered in the literature, the direct controller synthesis problem largely remains open. As the controlled system is generally a bilinear (instead of fully linear) Koopman model, controller synthesis appears to lose the linear--quadratic structures of the classical Lyapunov and Riccati methods for finite-dimensional linear systems. However, in infinite dimensions, bilinearity in the feature map should be merely artifactual and hence reducible to linearity in principle. In this work, by considering the operator semigroups in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space with a linear--Sobolev kernel and utilizing the Yosida approximation of their generators, the synthesis problems of a stabilizing controller and an input-unconstrained optimal controller can be formulated as an operator Lyapunov inequality and an operator Riccati equation, respectively. These formulations recover the desirable linear--quadratic structures, and hence, with sample data, they are solvable efficiently in analogous ways to usual linear systems by semidefinite programming solvers and Kleinman iterations, respectively. In addition to proving control performance bounds dependent on the sampling denseness and Yosida regularization, through numerical comparison to linearized LQR, bilinear EDMD-based synthesis, nonlinear MPC, and Koopman MPC methods on numerical models and process control examples, this work demonstrates the proposed Koopman--Riccati synthesis as a computationally efficient approach to obtain a near-optimal state-feedback control law.
tldr: The paper develops Koopman operator-based controller synthesis by formulating stabilizing controller design as an operator Lyapunov inequality and optimal control as an operator Riccati equation in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, solvable via SDP and Kleinman iterations.
motivation: Koopman lifted models of controlled nonlinear systems are bilinear, so classical linear-quadratic Lyapunov/Riccati synthesis does not directly apply; the author argues bilinearity is an artifact of the finite-dimensional feature map and can be reduced to linearity in infinite dimensions.
method: Operator semigroups on an RKHS with a linear-Sobolev kernel are used, with Yosida approximations of their generators, to derive operator Lyapunov inequalities and operator Riccati equations from sampled data.
result: Control performance bounds depending on sampling denseness and Yosida regularization are proven, and numerical comparisons against linearized LQR, bilinear EDMD synthesis, nonlinear MPC, and Koopman MPC show computationally efficient near-optimal state-feedback control.
conclusion: Koopman-Riccati synthesis recovers linear-quadratic structure in infinite dimensions and offers an efficient, near-optimal alternative to MPC-style approaches for nonlinear control.

title: A Good-Vorticity Low-Regularity Integrator For The Inviscid Oldroyd--B System With Stress Diffusion
authors: Xinyu Cheng, Zhaonan Luo, Zhaojie Yang, Cheng Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish sharp convergence results for a sequential semi-implicit good-vorticity integrator for the two-dimensional inviscid Oldroyd--B system with stress diffusion on the torus. For exact solutions satisfying [MATH] and [MATH], [MATH], we prove convergence in the critical norms [MATH], uniformly over the time nodes on every finite interval where these regularity assumptions hold, including the critical endpoint [MATH]. For [MATH], we obtain the rate [MATH] without any additional time H\"older assumption, reaching first order at [MATH]. These algebraic exponents are optimal for this Eulerian scheme over the stated solution classes, as shown by fixed-data lower bounds in the case [MATH] with nonzero velocity mean. For a fixed shear solution at critical regularity, we establish matching logarithmic upper and lower bounds on the numerical error, ruling out every positive algebraic convergence rate. We also prove that the gain of one stress derivative at the time nodes is optimal when the velocity is controlled in [MATH], even for smooth initial stress.
tldr: Sharp convergence and optimality results are proved for a semi-implicit 'good-vorticity' numerical integrator applied to the 2D inviscid Oldroyd-B system with stress diffusion.
motivation: The Oldroyd-B system models viscoelastic fluids, and reliable low-regularity numerical schemes with provable convergence rates are needed for critical-norm solution classes where standard smoothness assumptions fail.
method: A sequential semi-implicit good-vorticity time integrator is analyzed on the torus; convergence is established in critical norms uniformly in time, complemented by fixed-data lower bounds and matched logarithmic bounds for a critical shear solution.
result: Convergence is shown in critical norms including the endpoint case, with algebraic rates reaching first order at the critical regularity; these exponents are proved optimal via lower bounds, and a logarithmic error scaling is established for the critical shear solution.
conclusion: The scheme is sharp and optimal over the stated solution classes, and the gain of one stress derivative at time nodes is shown to be optimal; the work is purely numerical analysis of a fluid PDE system.

title: A Dual-Guided Column-Generation-Based Matheuristic For Integrated Railroad Blocking
authors: Yida Xu, Zhengzhong Ricky You, Baichuan Mo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.41403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated railroad blocking is a central planning problem in freight railway operations, which requires coordinated decisions on block design, blocking sequences, and block routing. We propose a dual-guided column-generation-based matheuristic (DG-CGM) that uses linear programming (LP) dual information to identify promising transportation paths and incorporates them into restricted mixed-integer programs to improve feasible solutions. Starting from an initial plan built by construction, DG-CGM alternates destroy and local repair with path generation, which uses dual prices from restricted LPs of a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation to identify promising transportation paths. When local improvements continue to stagnate, we further apply joint repair to combine alternatives across demand groups. To address the coupling between logical and physical path pricing, we introduce a joint reduced cost that eliminates path-specific dual variables from pricing, enabling more efficient column identification through exact labeling algorithms. We evaluate the performance of DG-CGM on both generated instances and real-world cases. On 150 generated instances with 50-150 nodes, DG-CGM achieves the optimal cost on 89 of the 91 instances solved to proven optimality by Gurobi, with a geometric mean runtime equal to 5.2% of that for Gurobi and a mean relative cost reduction of 3.4%. On six full-scale scenarios derived from the 2026 INFORMS Railway Applications Section competition data, each with 47,193 nodes, DG-CGM obtains feasible solutions within two hours that serve 95.9%-99.6% of the requested freight volume, providing practical blocking plans for large-scale railway operations. The code, instances, and computational results are publicly available at [URL].
tldr: The paper proposes a dual-guided column-generation-based matheuristic (DG-CGM) for integrated railroad blocking in freight railway operations, combining LP dual information with destroy-and-repair local search and exact labeling-based pricing.
